citation: CHANGED for INVENTION and a verdict-altering false finding in the sslVersions test. (1) The reviewed regex ^\s*(tls1\.2|\*\s*,\s*-ssl3\s*,\s*-tls1\.0\s*,\s*-tls1\.1)\s*$ admits exactly two spellings and rejects hardened values the specification explicitly permits. Tested against the reviewed pattern, all three of 'tls1.2,-ssl3', '*,-ssl2,-ssl3,-tls1.0,-tls1.1' and 'tls,-ssl3,-tls1.0,-tls1.1' fail, yet web.conf.spec:245 and server.conf.spec:772-773 state that '-ssl2 is accepted in the version list but does nothing', and :242-244 and :769 make 'tls' a legitimate positive term. An instance hardened with the -ssl2 spelling, which is the form the vendor's own default files have historically carried, would be written up as a finding with no weak protocol enabled anywhere. The replacement is a two-condition property test, both halves anchored so it behaves identically under re.search and re.fullmatch: the first restricts the list's positive term and confines the rest to exclusions, the second requires all three weak versions to be excluded whenever the positive term is a wildcard. Verified over 18 values: it passes tls1.2, tls1.2 with exclusions, '*,-ssl3,-tls1.0,-tls1.1' in both spaced and unspaced form, '*,-ssl2,-ssl3,-tls1.0,-tls1.1' and 'tls,-ssl3,-tls1.0,-tls1.1'; it fails '*', 'tls', '*,-ssl2', '*,-ssl3,-tls1.0', 'tls1.1', 'ssl3', 'tls1.0,tls1.2', 'tls1.2,tls1.1' and the empty value. Note for maintenance, not a defect: the spec set shipped here lists only ssl3, tls1.0, tls1.1 and tls1.2 (web.conf.spec:241, server.conf.spec:767), so a value of tls1.3 fails both patterns; if a later maintenance release adds tls1.3 to the vocabulary the first pattern must be widened, or this criterion will fail a stronger configuration. (2) SPLUNK_FIPS equals:1 is outside the vocabulary the authority itself uses: splunk-launch.conf.spec:110 declares [0|1] but :115 and :119-120 instruct the operator to set it to 'true', so an instance configured exactly as the specification directs would fail. Relaxed to in:1|true. (3) No scope change: every condition remains a Splunk configuration value, and the kernel and module dependency plus the one-time install constraint are stated in external_dependencies so remediation is not misrepresented as a live configuration edit.

citation: CHANGED for OVER-REACH and for the same sslVersions regex defect corrected under SRG-APP-000014-WSR-000006. (1) The condition 'server.conf [sslConfig] sslVerifyServerCert in:1|true' has been removed. Per server.conf.spec:798-823 this setting governs splunkd acting as a TLS client validating a certificate that a server presents to it, named there for distributed search and deployment-client polling, and its default is false (:823). It therefore decides nothing about the integrity of a remote user's session with this web server, which is what CCI-001453 and this check text address; it belongs to the requirement on authenticating communicating peers. Because the default is false, the reviewed criterion would record a finding against a standalone instance whose Splunk Web sessions are fully TLS protected, and the remediation it implies is operationally loaded: server.conf.spec:1189-1190 warns that enabling peer verification requires [sslConfig]/sslRootCAPath to be correct first, so an assessor acting on this row could break distributed search while closing a row that was never open. This is not an external dependency and has not been recorded as one, because it is an application setting; it is simply assessed under a different requirement. (2) The sslVersions operand has been replaced with the same verified two-condition property test, for the reasons and with the test results given under SRG-APP-000014-WSR-000006; the reviewed single pattern rejected 'tls1.2,-ssl3', '*,-ssl2,-ssl3,-tls1.0,-tls1.1' and 'tls,-ssl3,-tls1.0,-tls1.1', all permitted by web.conf.spec:239-245. (3) Scope boundary stated explicitly: the inventory rows for this requirement carry no server.conf key that enables TLS on the splunkd management listener, so this criterion covers the Splunk Web listener only. That is the honest limit of the row and it must not be papered over by testing sslVerifyServerCert instead. requireClientCert (web.conf.spec:151-165) is likewise left out: mutual certificate authentication is an optional method, not a condition of integrity protection, and requiring it would fail compliant deployments.

application_contribution: Splunk enforces logical access through roles defined in authorize.conf: each role enumerates its capabilities and may scope the indexes it can search, the indexes it cannot, a search filter imposed on it, and the roles it may grant. citation: CHANGED for INVENTION and a verdict-altering false finding. The reviewed criterion decided a high-severity access control requirement on the single condition 'authorize.conf [role_<roleName>] srchIndexesAllowed non_empty'. That condition fails roles that are correctly configured. srchIndexesAllowed has no default (authorize.conf.spec:295), and the specification provides two other ways to scope the same access: srchIndexesDisallowed, which :299-301 states takes precedence over srchIndexesAllowed, and srchFilter at :150. A role that restricts access by exclusion or by filter, and a role that carries only interface capabilities and needs no search access at all, both report the key absent and would be written up as findings although nothing is wrong with them. The reviewed criterion also invents the organization's list: the task rule on organization-defined values says the criterion is what the product must be able to express, not a value the assessor supplies, and which indexes belong to which role is precisely an organization-defined list. The replacement tests what configuration can decide, that access is expressed through roles (authorize.conf.spec:67-78), and records the relevance judgment where it is actually carried, in external_dependencies. One point on evaluator semantics, which this correction depends on and which also governs SRG-APP-000033-WSR-000169, SRG-APP-000291-AU-000200 and SRG-APP-000292-AU-000420: conditions written against a wildcard stanza name such as [role_<roleName>] or savedsearches.conf [<search name>] must be evaluated existentially, satisfied when at least one stanza meets the whole condition set. Evaluated universally, 'srchIndexesAllowed non_empty' fails on Splunk's own shipped roles and the scheduled-notification conditions fail on Splunk's own shipped saved searches, which would make those criteria unsatisfiable by any instance, and a criterion nothing can satisfy is a defect rather than a strict standard. No condition here reads anything outside Splunk configuration.

citation: CHANGED for INVENTION. The condition 'web.conf [settings] enableCertBasedUserAuth present' has been removed. Per web.conf.spec:120-131 that setting selects whether splunkd uses a digital certificate to identify a user, and :125 requires requireClientCert to be true alongside it; it governs how an identity is established, not whether an established identity is authorized for the content it requested, which is the whole of this check text. The operand appears in neither the check text nor the fix text, and no product STIG rule shares this CCI. It is also inert as a test: the setting has a default of false (web.conf.spec:131), so in the merged configuration the assessment reads it is always present and the condition can never fail, which leaves a reader of the checklist with certificate-based authentication cited as the criterion for an authorization requirement and no evidence behind it. certBasedUserAuthMethod and requireClientCert are left out for the same reason, with the role mapping that external providers drive recorded in external_dependencies. The wildcard-stanza evaluation rule given under SRG-APP-000033-AU-001610 applies to the remaining condition: it is satisfied when at least one [role_<roleName>] stanza is present.

Whether the role an identity receives is the correct one for the content requested is fixed by the organization's access control policy, not by any Splunk setting.
finding_statement: Splunk Enterprise does not define the roles in authorize.conf against which Splunk Web performs its authorization check, so no application-layer authorization decision stands between an authenticated identity and the requested content.

citation: CHANGED for INVENTION. The condition 'authentication.conf [splunk_auth] lockoutMins present' has been removed. lockoutMins is the lockout duration, the number of minutes a user stays locked out after the limit is reached (authentication.conf.spec:521-530, default 30). This requirement is CCI-000044 / AC-7 a, the limit on consecutive invalid attempts; the duration of the lockout is a different control enhancement and belongs to the requirement that addresses it. The operand appears in neither the SRG check text nor the product STIG fix text for SPLK-CL-000060, whose fix sets only lockoutAttempts and lockoutThresholdMins, and because lockoutMins has a default it reads as present in every merged configuration, so the condition can never fail and adds no evidence while attributing another requirement's objective to this row. The two numeric directions were checked against the product STIG check text and are correct as written and retained: lockoutAttempts takes max:3 because more than 3 is a finding, lockoutThresholdMins takes min:15 because less than 15 is a finding, and each correctly fails the vendor default of 5 (authentication.conf.spec:541, :552). lockoutUsers is retained on the specification's own terms, since authentication.conf.spec:514-519 makes it the switch that gives the other two settings effect, and in:1|true accepts either boolean spelling.

application_contribution: Splunk Enterprise has no inactivity timer of its own over the native account store, but it does hold the inbound provisioning path by which an identity provider that detects 35 days of inactivity applies the deactivation to the account this instance holds: splunkd launches the supervisor process that handles SCIM authorization tokens, and Splunk Web exposes the automated user management controls that configure it. Keeping that path available is the application's share.
citation: ADDED, not corrected: this requirement is present in inventory/groups/AC-1.json as the seventeenth member of the group and carries an APPLICABLE determination in inventory/sca-determinations.json, but no criterion was derived for it, so the row would stay not_reviewed with nothing recorded about what the application can and cannot do. The criterion follows the two settings the determination names and that inventory/checks.tsv already carries as declared keys. Both are deliberately written against their vendor defaults, which are the permissive state: server.conf.spec:6591 gives disabled a default of false and web-features.conf.spec:409 gives enabled a default of true, so the criterion passes an instance that has left the provisioning path intact and fails only one that has explicitly turned it off. Written the other way round, as a demand that an organization adopt SCIM provisioning, it would be over-reach, since a site using only native local accounts has no Splunk setting that disables an account for inactivity and would be failed for a lever the product does not provide. The third key in the inventory row, authentication.conf scimSupportedDomains, is excluded on two grounds: checks.tsv marks it undeclared, and it is absent from the specification set provided here, so no vocabulary or default can be cited for it. Caution on citations generally, from the same determination: the provided specification snapshot is shorter than the set 10.4.2 ships and the line numbers diverge, [teleport_supervisor] sitting at snapshot line 6584 against shipped line 6998 and [splunk_auth] at snapshot 437 against shipped 458. Every file:line in this review resolves against the snapshot supplied as the input, and any criterion republished against a shipped instance must have its citations re-resolved.

conditions.rationale: server.conf.spec:6584-6591: disabled = true means splunkd does not launch the supervisor process that "handles authorization tokens for System for Cross-Domain Identity Management (SCIM) operations"; default false, so this condition fails only an instance that has explicitly foreclosed the provisioning path

external_dependencies: The 35-day inactivity determination is made by the organization's directory service or SAML identity provider, which must then apply the deactivation to this instance over SCIM; that component is assessed under its own baseline.

The native account store exposes no inactivity timer. authentication.conf.spec:487 expirePasswordDays and :504 expireUserAccounts govern password expiry, not account inactivity, so where a site relies on native local accounts the requirement is carried by an organizational account-review procedure.

The account of last resort that the fix text exempts is identified by the organization; its role-scoped counterparts are authorize.conf.spec:867 [capability::never_lockout] and :870 [capability::never_expire].
finding_statement: Splunk Enterprise has disabled the SCIM provisioning path through which an identity provider applies an inactivity-triggered deactivation, so the application has foreclosed the only mechanism by which it can contribute to disabling accounts after 35 days of inactivity; the inactivity determination itself rests with the identity provider and, for native local accounts, with an organizational account-review procedure.
manual_reason: Splunk Enterprise exposes no setting that tracks last successful logon per account or disables an account after a period of inactivity; the lockout settings in authentication.conf act on consecutive failed logons, not on inactivity, and the SCIM and Automated User Management settings only permit an external identity source to carry out a deprovisioning decision made elsewhere. The 35-day determination therefore cannot be read from Splunk configuration, and failing the application for it would be a false finding.

citation: Both original conditions were defective. (1) srchIndexesAllowed non_empty is the wrong direction: an unset or empty allow-list is the restrictive case (authorize.conf.spec:292-295, "No default"), so the condition failed exactly the locked-down role and passed every role that had been granted index access. (2) not_in *|_* misreads the wildcard vocabulary. Per authorize.conf.spec:284-288, "*" does not match internal indexes, so the shipped role_user and role_power value of "*" (authorize.conf:234, 274) already cannot reach _audit or _internal - yet the condition failed both - while role_admin's shipped "*;_*" (authorize.conf:404) is literally neither "*" nor "_*" and passed, which is the one role that can read the audit trail. The replacement tests the underscore boundary itself. It is pinned to the two shipped general-purpose role stanzas rather than written over [role_<roleName>] because a wildcard stanza would fail role_admin on every install, and the admin role is an authorized reader; which other roles are authorized is organization-defined and is recorded as an external dependency.

citation: restmap.conf capability.post present and capability.put present are removed for the reason given on SRG-APP-000121-AU-000130: the keys are real (restmap.conf.spec:111-112, 303-312) but the stanza exists only where an app declares its own endpoint, so the conditions fail a conformant deployment that declares none. admin_all_objects absent read over [role_<roleName>] fails every install, because the shipped role_admin holds it and must (authorize.conf:290); pinning it to the general-purpose roles keeps the test and removes the false finding. change_audit is added because it is the product's own named gate on changing audit settings and, like admin_all_objects, ships to role_admin alone, so the condition passes stock and fails a genuine grant.

conditions.rationale: check text: "protect audit tools from unauthorized modification"; authorize.conf.spec:447-453 - the capability bypasses every access control list, which includes write access to the objects that serve as audit tools.
same reading applied to the second shipped general-purpose role (shipped on role_admin only, authorize.conf:290).

authorize.conf.spec:483-485 - change_audit "Lets a user change audit settings through the audit endpoints" and "reload audit settings", which is modification of the audit tooling itself; shipped on role_admin only (authorize.conf:293).
same reading applied to the second shipped general-purpose role.

external_dependencies: Write permissions on the Splunk binaries and application directories - SPLK-CL-000190 implements this at the operating system layer
Object-level write access recorded in default.meta, which the btool-based collector does not read
finding_statement: A general-purpose role holds admin_all_objects or change_audit, so the audit tools or the audit configuration can be modified by an account that is not privileged.

application_contribution: Deleting a saved search, report or configuration object that serves as an audit tool requires write access to it or the capability that bypasses access control lists, so the application's share is that this capability stays off the general-purpose roles.
citation: restmap.conf capability.delete present is removed for the reason given on SRG-APP-000121-AU-000130 - the stanza exists only where an app declares its own REST endpoint, so the condition fails a conformant deployment that declares none. admin_all_objects absent over [role_<roleName>] fails every install because the shipped role_admin holds it (authorize.conf:290); pinned to the two shipped general-purpose roles it passes stock and fails a real grant.

conditions.rationale: check text: "protect audit tools from unauthorized deletion"; authorize.conf.spec:447-453 - the capability bypasses every access control list, which is what otherwise prevents deletion of another role's objects.
same reading applied to the second shipped general-purpose role (shipped on role_admin only, authorize.conf:290).

external_dependencies: Delete permissions on the Splunk binaries and installation directories - SPLK-CL-000190 implements this at the operating system layer
Object-level write access recorded in default.meta, which the btool-based collector does not read

application_contribution: Where the organization chooses to use them, Splunk can place a second copy of the indexed records off the indexing instance through a frozen archive destination (coldToFrozenDir or coldToFrozenScript), remote store-backed indexes (remotePath), or index replication in a cluster, and the assessor records which is in use as evidence rather than as a pass condition.
citation: server.conf [clustering] replication_factor min 2 is removed: server.conf.spec:2929-2935 makes the setting valid only for "mode=manager" with a default of 3, so a single-instance indexer and a cluster peer alike have no such setting and would be failed for not running a feature the requirement never asks for. coldToFrozenDir non_empty is removed for the same class of error: it fails a stock install whose backups are taken with the operating system tool SPLK-CL-000250 names. Because conditions are ANDed, the pair also demanded index clustering and a frozen archive at the same time, which no single deployment shape satisfies.
external_dependencies: The seven-day backup schedule, the backup tool and the medium - SPLK-CL-000250 assigns all three to the operating system backup tool or another approved tool
Confirmation that the destination is a different system or component, which the application cannot establish about a path or endpoint handed to it
finding_statement: No backup of the log records repository onto a different system or component is in place; the application's optional off-instance copy levers are not a substitute for the backup process the requirement names.
manual_reason: The benchmark authority implements this requirement outside the application: SPLK-CL-000250's check is an interview with the system administrator and its fix directs "the underlying OS backup tools, or another approved backup tool". Splunk has optional levers that place a second copy off the indexing instance, but none that the authority requires, so any condition over them fails a deployment that is backed up exactly as directed.

application_contribution: The application expresses how long indexed records are held before they roll to frozen, which is the only part of this requirement a Splunk setting reaches, and it can be held to the seven-day floor the check text states.
citation: frozenTimePeriodInSecs present cannot fail: indexes.conf.spec:691 gives a default of 188697600, so btool reports the key on every index and the criterion returned a green status that was not evidence. The requirement does state one number the product can be held to - the seven-day non-SAMI floor - and that is not an organization-defined value being invented here but the check text's own words, so a lower bound is both derivable and falsifiable. The five-year figure applies to the backup medium rather than to the index and stays an external dependency.

conditions.rationale: check text: "a minimum of 7 days for non-SAMI"; 604800 seconds is seven days, and indexes.conf.spec:684-691 defines the setting as the seconds after which indexed data rolls to frozen. "min" is the direction the words "a minimum of" give.

external_dependencies: Selection of backup media capable of guaranteeing file integrity for a minimum of five years, which no Splunk setting expresses
Retention of the backups themselves and the five-year SAMI period, documented in the SSP and carried by the backup tool SPLK-CL-000250 names
finding_statement: An index is configured to roll data to frozen in less than seven days, so the application does not hold the records for the minimum period the requirement states for non-SAMI.

application_contribution: Where the organization uses them, the frozen archive destination (coldToFrozenDir or coldToFrozenScript) and remote store-backed indexes (remotePath) put a copy of the indexed Splunk Web records on other media, and the assessor records which is in use as evidence.
citation: coldToFrozenDir non_empty was the only condition, and it fails a stock install for a setting that indexes.conf.spec:792-802 presents as one alternative among several and that the product STIG does not require. Reporting a finding there would charge the application for a backup the benchmark authority itself assigns to an operating system tool.
external_dependencies: The backup onto different media and its schedule - SPLK-CL-000250 assigns both to the operating system backup tool or another approved tool
Confirmation that the medium is unrelated to the system being logged, which the application cannot establish about a path handed to it
finding_statement: No backup of the Splunk Web log records onto a different system or media is in place; the application's optional archive destination is not a substitute for the backup process the requirement names.
manual_reason: Splunk Web's records reach the internal indexes, and SPLK-CL-000250 places their backup on "the underlying OS backup tools, or another approved backup tool" with an interview as its check. The application has optional off-instance copy levers but none the authority requires, so no configuration read can decide this requirement without failing a deployment that is backed up as directed.

application_contribution: Audit reduction and on-demand reporting are native Splunk search functions; what the application configures is the reporting content itself - saved searches with a defined search string and a bounded dispatch window, supported by search macros, data model acceleration and metric rollup policies.
citation: SRG-APP-000181-AU-000200 (V-206483) check text; savedsearches.conf.spec:44, 564-570; datamodels.conf.spec:29-40; macros.conf.spec:52; metric_rollups.conf.spec:38-48

conditions.rationale: "search = <string>" is the saved search itself (savedsearches.conf.spec:44) - on-demand reporting over the audit data is expressed as at least one saved report.
A dispatch window declared with no value bounds nothing, so the test is on the value rather than on the key.

external_dependencies: The organization's on-demand reporting requirements - which reports are required, over which fields, and for which recipients - which the check text leaves organization-defined and no Splunk setting supplies
Review of the report output by the responsible staff
finding_statement: No saved report with a defined search string and dispatch window exists over the audit data, so the application carries no configured audit reduction to support the organization's on-demand reporting requirements.

application_contribution: Splunk expresses its own log storage allocation in several places it configures: a size ceiling per index, a free-space floor that pauses indexing, and explicit size and generation counts on the Splunk Web and splunkd stderr logs.
citation: The four web.conf min 1 conditions point the wrong way for a capacity requirement: web.conf.spec:878 and 893 state that 0, or the setting commented out, means unlimited file size, so min 1 fails exactly the configuration that allows the most storage and passes a one-byte ceiling. Since the size is organization-defined against SP 800-92, the criterion is that the product expresses the allocation. indexes.conf [volume:<name>] maxVolumeDataSizeMB present is removed: indexes.conf.spec:2078-2091 marks it Optional and ignores it on remote storage, so a deployment that defines no volume stanza has nothing to read and would be failed for not using an optional feature. maxTotalDataSizeMB, the per-index allocation the determination for this requirement names, is the lever that always exists. Note for the inventory rather than the criterion: checks.tsv lost maxTotalDataSizeMB, homePath.maxDataSizeMB and coldPath.maxDataSizeMB here because parse-mechanisms.py cuts the key list at the first "]" it finds in the mechanism text, so keys written before the stanza are dropped.

conditions.rationale: check text requires that record storage capacity be allocated "in accordance with specifications within NIST SP 800-92", an organization-defined size, so the criterion is that the product expresses the per-index allocation (indexes.conf.spec:610-613).
web.conf.spec:876-882 - the ceiling on web_access.log; the value is organization-defined against SP 800-92, so the criterion is that it is expressed.
web.conf.spec:884-889 - the number of generations retained alongside the size ceiling.
web.conf.spec:891-897 - the ceiling on web_service.log.
web.conf.spec:899-905 - the generations retained for web_service.log.
server.conf.spec:1686-1692 - the rotation ceiling on splunkd_stderr.log, described as the way to "allocate less storage to this log category".
server.conf.spec:1694-1700 - "How many rolled copies to keep" for that log.
non_empty cannot fail against the shipped 5000 MB default, so the operand admits the percentage form the 25-percent floor needs, or a deliberate megabyte floor of 10000 MB or more.

external_dependencies: The size of the partitions and storage volumes presented to Splunk, provisioned at the operating system and storage layer, which is what the allocation is measured against
The organization's SP 800-92 sizing figures, which no product setting supplies
finding_statement: The application does not express its log storage allocation - a per-index size ceiling, a free-space floor, or the size and generation counts on the Splunk Web and splunkd stderr logs is unset - so the capacity allocated to log records is not configured.

application_contribution: Splunk off-loads log records through outputs.conf, where the target group names the receiving systems, and that naming is the whole of the application's share.
citation: outputs.conf [tcpout] defaultGroup non_empty is a false finding. outputs.conf.spec:63-70 states "If you don't want to forward data automatically, don't configure this setting", that it is overridden by _TCP_ROUTING in inputs.conf, and that "Starting with version 4.2, this setting is no longer required" - so a deployment that routes per input forwards correctly with no defaultGroup at all. The setting also appears in neither the check text nor the fix text, and in no checks.tsv row for this requirement. One caution on the condition kept: outputs.conf.spec:128 makes server "Required if the 'indexerDiscovery' setting is not set", so a target group that discovers its receivers satisfies the requirement without it. The vocabulary has no way to express that alternative, so it is recorded as an external dependency and the assessor must accept indexerDiscovery as equivalent.

conditions.rationale: SPLK-CL-000150 check text: "check that the outputs.conf file is configured with the details of the source that the logs will be sent to (e.g. Hostname, port# etc.)"; outputs.conf.spec:123-133 defines server as that list of receiving systems.

external_dependencies: The receiving indexer or external repository and its own inputs.conf - SPLK-CL-000150 places that configuration on a separate machine, "which is always a separate machine regardless of environment"
The requirement's own not-applicable clause where an external application or the operating system performs the off-load
Where a target group uses indexerDiscovery instead of a static server list, the cluster manager that supplies the receivers
finding_statement: No forwarding target group names a receiving system, so the application is not configured to off-load its log records to another system.

application_contribution: The application's contribution is that its path to an audit log server is configured and unobstructed: a target group names the receiving systems it writes to.
citation: defaultGroup non_empty is removed for the reason given on SRG-APP-000358-AU-000100: outputs.conf.spec:63-70 makes it optional, overridable by _TCP_ROUTING, and "no longer required" since 4.2, so the condition failed deployments that forward correctly through per-input routing. The indexerDiscovery alternative to a static server list (outputs.conf.spec:128) is recorded as an external dependency because the vocabulary cannot express an either-or condition.

conditions.rationale: SPLK-CL-000150 check text: outputs.conf carries "the details of the source that the logs will be sent to (e.g. Hostname, port# etc.)"; outputs.conf.spec:123-133.

external_dependencies: The audit log server itself, its receiving port and its storage - SPLK-CL-000150 places the matching inputs.conf on a separate instance
The test the check text describes, in which a user generates events and the data is observed arriving on the separate server, which is an operator procedure rather than a configuration read
Where a target group uses indexerDiscovery instead of a static server list, the cluster manager that supplies the receivers
finding_statement: No forwarding target group names a receiving system, so the application cannot write or transfer its log records to a separate audit log server.

application_contribution: Splunk integrates with surrounding security infrastructure in two configurable ways: it forwards its events onward through outputs.conf, and it fires alert actions from its own health reporter. The existence of the receiving security tool is not a Splunk setting.
citation: SRG-APP-000358-WSR-000163 (V-206423) check text; SPLK-CL-000150 check and fix text; outputs.conf.spec:121-131; health.conf.spec:217-219

conditions.rationale: "A comma-separated list of one or more systems to send data to over a TCP socket. ... Typically used to specify receiving Splunk systems, although you can use it to send data to non-Splunk systems (see the 'sendCookedData' setting)." (outputs.conf.spec:121-131) - this is the application's path for sending logged events to another security tool, and is the check SPLK-CL-000150 names.

"disabled = [0|1] * A value of 1 disables this alert action. * Default: 0 (enabled)" (health.conf.spec:217-219) - the alert capability the requirement asks for must be enabled for the configured action.

external_dependencies: The organization's security tool that offers review and alert capability, and its own ingestion configuration
Whether that tool is in place at all, which the check text asks the assessor to determine and no Splunk setting records
Network reachability and transport between Splunk and that tool
finding_statement: No receiving system is configured in outputs.conf and the health reporter's alert action is disabled, so the application sends its logged events and alerts nowhere and is not integrated with the organization's security infrastructure.

application_contribution: Splunk carries this requirement in the product through the health reporter: minFreeSpace sets the storage floor, the disk_space indicator thresholds fire at one and two multiples of it, and the email alert action carries the notification to a recipient list.
citation: Four corrections. (1) health.conf [feature:disk_space] alert.actions non_empty is outside that stanza's vocabulary: the specification documents alert.actions only under [health_reporter] (health.conf.spec:93), while [feature:*] takes alert.disabled, alert.min_duration_sec, alert.threshold_color and the per-indicator alert:<indicator name>.* forms (spec:165-211). The shipped file sets alert.actions = email in [health_reporter] (health.conf:27) and in no feature stanza, so the condition failed every install for a key that stanza does not have - note too that checks.tsv marks the key "declared" because parse-mechanisms.py tests key names per file rather than per stanza. (2) alert.threshold_color in yellow|red cannot fail: those are the only two values the setting accepts (spec:101-103, default red). It is replaced by the two switches that can fail - the global alert.disabled and the feature's own override. (3) alert.min_duration_sec present is vacuous against the shipped 60 and leaves the one direction that matters untested: this requirement says "immediate", and a larger value defers the notification, so an upper bound at the product's own documented default is the condition that decides it. (4) The external dependency on volume size is overstated: server.conf.spec:1858-1866 permits a percentage, so minFreeSpace = 25% expresses the fix text's figure without any reading from the storage layer.

conditions.rationale: SPLK-CL-000160 fix text: "[alert_action:email] disabled = 0"; health.conf.spec:217-221.

SPLK-CL-000160 fix text: "Set the email addresses of the ISSO and SA to be able to receive alerts"; the shipped health.conf leaves action.to empty (health.conf:34), so this condition carries real evidence.
health.conf.spec:88-91 - "If the value is set to 1, alerting for all features is disabled", the switch that would silence the alert the fix text configures.
health.conf.spec:93-94 - "The alert actions that will run when an alert is fired", documented only in this stanza; the shipped file sets alert.actions = email here (health.conf:27).
health.conf.spec:165-171 - a feature can disable its own alerting; expressed as not_equals so that a feature which does not set the key still satisfies the condition.
SPLK-CL-000160 fix text: "Set the Red setting to 1"; health.conf.spec:196-201 and health.conf:291.
SPLK-CL-000160 fix text: "Yellow setting to 2"; health.conf.spec:196-201 and health.conf:292.

check text: "send an immediate warning to the SA and ISSO"; health.conf.spec:96-99 makes this the delay the status color must persist before an alert fires, with a product default of 60, so the notification must not be deferred beyond the product's own default.
non_empty cannot fail against the shipped 5000 MB default, so the operand admits the percentage form the 25-percent floor needs, or a deliberate megabyte floor of 10000 MB or more.

external_dependencies: SMTP relay reachability and mail delivery, which depend on the mail server and the network
The ISSO and SA recipient addresses, which the organization supplies

The size of the storage volume, needed only to confirm an absolute minFreeSpace value in megabytes; a percentage value expresses the fix text's 25 percent in the product and needs nothing from outside it
finding_statement: The application's storage alert is incomplete: the free-space floor, the health reporter's alerting, the email recipient list, or the disk_space indicator thresholds are not configured to raise an immediate notification as storage approaches capacity.

application_contribution: The application sets its own storage floor in server.conf and can raise a scheduled alert with an email recipient list as capacity is approached; both the floor and the alert are configured in the product.
citation: web.conf log.access_maxsize min 1 is removed on two counts: nothing in the check text or the fix text ties a web access log rotation ceiling to a 75 percent capacity warning, and web.conf.spec:878 makes 0 mean unlimited, so the bound fails the largest allocation. enableSched is added because savedsearches.conf.spec:73-77 defaults it to 0: the criterion as written reported a satisfied alert path - condition set, recipient set - for a saved search that never runs. One limitation to record: the three savedsearches conditions are independent per-key tests and the schema cannot bind them to one stanza, so the assessor must confirm they describe the same saved search.

conditions.rationale: fix text: the ISSO and SA addresses receive the warning; savedsearches.conf.spec:304-307 marks action.email.to REQUIRED for the email action with an empty default.
check text requires that a warning be provided; savedsearches.conf.spec:73-77 defaults enableSched to 0, so an alert that is not scheduled never runs and never warns.
non_empty cannot fail against the shipped 5000 MB default, so the operand admits the percentage form the 25-percent floor needs, or a deliberate megabyte floor of 10000 MB or more.

external_dependencies: SMTP relay reachability and mail delivery, which depend on the mail server and the network
The ISSO and SA recipient addresses, which the organization supplies
The size of the storage volume, needed only to confirm an absolute minFreeSpace value; a percentage value expresses 25 percent in the product

Which saved search carries the trigger, which is organization-defined content: a trigger is expressed either by alert_condition or by counttype with relation and quantity, so a test on alert_condition alone reports a finding against a search that is correctly configured the other way.
finding_statement: The application has no enabled, scheduled alert with a recipient list that warns as log record storage approaches capacity, or its free-space floor is unset.

application_contribution: Splunk carries this with its own reporting and notification tools, which is what the product STIG directs: a scheduled search over the audit data with an alert condition and an email recipient list, and the health reporter's alerting wired to an action.
citation: Two corrections. savedsearches.conf realtime_schedule in 1|true is both vacuous and a misreading: savedsearches.conf.spec:137-155 defaults it to true and describes it as how the scheduler computes the next run time, not whether the alert is real time, and spec:151 directs continuous scheduling (false) whenever summary indexing is enabled - so the condition could fail a legitimate configuration while never catching an alert that is not scheduled at all. enableSched, which defaults to 0 (spec:73-77), is the setting that decides that. health.conf [feature:*] alert.actions non_empty is outside the feature stanza's vocabulary: alert.actions is documented only under [health_reporter] (health.conf.spec:93) and the shipped file sets it there (health.conf:27), so the condition failed every install; read over [feature:*] it also demanded an action on the three dozen shipped features that have nothing to do with audit failure, two of which ship with alerting disabled (health.conf:74, 83).

conditions.rationale: SPLK-CL-000170 fix text: "using the reporting and notification tools, to create a report with notification to the SA and ISSO of any audit failure events".
SPLK-CL-000170 fix text: notification to the SA and ISSO; savedsearches.conf.spec:304-307 marks action.email.to REQUIRED for the email action.
savedsearches.conf.spec:73-77 - enableSched defaults to 0 and is what decides whether the notification runs at all.
health.conf.spec:88-91 - "If the value is set to 1, alerting for all features is disabled", which would silence the health reporter's own audit-failure indicators.
health.conf.spec:93-94 - the actions that run when a health alert fires; documented only in this stanza.

external_dependencies: SMTP relay reachability and delivery within seconds, which depends on the mail server and the network rather than on Splunk
The SA and ISSO recipient addresses, which the organization supplies
Which hosts and devices are within the scope of coverage, and the ISSO's confirmation of receipt that SPLK-CL-000170 obtains by interview

Which saved search carries the trigger, which is organization-defined content: a trigger is expressed either by alert_condition or by counttype with relation and quantity, so a test on alert_condition alone reports a finding against a search that is correctly configured the other way.
finding_statement: The application has no enabled, scheduled alert with a recipient list over audit failure events, or health reporter alerting is turned off, so loss of communications or a halt in received records raises no notification.

application_contribution: Sorting log records is a native Splunk search command and needs no configuration, so the application's share is that the saved content the organization sorts with exists in the product.
citation: fields.conf [<field name>] INDEXED present is removed. fields.conf.spec:89-94 makes it a boolean defaulting to false and states that search-time extraction "accounts for the majority of fields", so the condition failed twice over: present is satisfied by INDEXED = false and therefore decides nothing, and requiring an index-time field declaration before a record can be sorted fails the ordinary Splunk deployment, which extracts at search time. Sorting itself needs no configuration, and which fields are of interest is organization-defined, so no condition can carry that part; it is recorded as an external dependency instead.

conditions.rationale: check text: "perform on-demand sorting of log records for events of interest based on the content of organization-defined audit fields" - the search content, including any sort expression, is what the product stores.

external_dependencies: The organization's definition of which audit fields are of interest, which the check text leaves organization-defined and no product setting supplies
The field extractions the organization writes for its own sources (props.conf EXTRACT- and REPORT- classes with transforms.conf), whose content is specific to the data it collects
finding_statement: The product stores no saved search content for audit review, so the organization's sorting of its audit fields is not expressed in the application.

application_contribution: Searching is the product's core function; what the application configures is that the general-purpose role which audit reviewers hold retains the search capability and an index grant to search with.
citation: Both conditions were written over [role_<roleName>], which makes them undecidable rather than strict. Read over every role they fail the shipped role_can_delete, which carries neither key (authorize.conf:240-248), and capabilities and index grants are inherited through importRoles (authorize.conf.spec:73-74, 79-84), so a role that holds search by inheritance - role_power imports user - has no line to read and would be failed for a capability it holds. Read instead as "at least one role" they pass trivially on every install and are not evidence. Pinning both to the shipped general-purpose role, where each key is always present in btool output, gives a condition that can only fail where the capability or the grant has actually been removed.

conditions.rationale: check text: "performs on-demand searches of log records for events of interest"; authorize.conf.spec:953 defines the search capability and spec:68-72 makes "enabled" the only accepted value. The shipped role_user carries it (authorize.conf:220), so the condition fails only where searching has been withdrawn.

authorize.conf.spec:292-295 - the list of indexes the role may search; the shipped value is "*" (authorize.conf:234). Here a non-empty grant is the direction the requirement wants, unlike SRG-APP-000118 where a grant is the weakening.

external_dependencies: The organization's definition of the events of interest and the audit fields that identify them, which the check text leaves organization-defined
Which roles the organization's audit reviewers hold, and any custom role it defines in place of the shipped ones
finding_statement: The general-purpose role no longer holds the search capability or has no index grant, so on-demand searching of log records is not available to the accounts that perform audit review.

application_contribution: Splunk performs audit reduction with data model acceleration, report acceleration, summary indexing and metric rollups. The application's share is that the review and analysis artifacts exist over the audit data and that the acceleration decision for them is stated rather than left implicit.
citation: SRG-APP-000364-AU-000190 (V-206497) check text; savedsearches.conf.spec:44, 439-447, 767-790; datamodels.conf.spec:29-40, 100-104; metric_rollups.conf.spec:38-48

conditions.rationale: "search = <string>" (savedsearches.conf.spec:44) - the on-demand review and analysis content is expressed as at least one saved search over the audit data.

"Whether or not the Splunk platform automatically accelerates this data model. Automatic acceleration creates auxiliary column stores for the fields and values in the events for this data model on a per-bucket basis. ... Default: false" (datamodels.conf.spec:29-40). Acceleration is the product's audit reduction mechanism; the criterion requires the decision be stated, because enabling it is an organization sizing choice - summary indexing and auto_summarize are the equivalent forms (savedsearches.conf.spec:439-447, 767-790).

external_dependencies: The organization's audit review and analysis procedure, who performs it and how often, which no product setting records
Disk capacity for the acceleration column stores, provisioned at the storage layer
finding_statement: No saved search exists over the audit data and no acceleration or summarization decision is expressed, so the application carries no configured audit reduction to support on-demand review and analysis.

application_contribution: After-the-fact investigation needs the records to still be reachable, so the application's share is the retention period it holds indexed data for before rolling it to frozen.
citation: coldToFrozenDir non_empty is removed: indexes.conf.spec:792-802 presents the archive destination as one alternative to a script, nothing in the check text or the fix text requires an archive, and the condition failed a stock install. It also contradicted this criterion's own external dependency, which already assigns thawing and the archive medium to an operator procedure - a condition and an external dependency over the same thing is how a checklist charges the application twice for one objective.

conditions.rationale: check text: "audit reduction that supports after-the-fact investigations of security incidents" - the period is organization-defined, so the criterion is that the product expresses it (indexes.conf.spec:684-691).

external_dependencies: Thawing archived buckets back into a searchable index, an operator procedure outside the product's configuration
The medium that holds any frozen archive, and the organization's investigation procedure itself
finding_statement: The application does not express a retention period for indexed records, so there is no configured basis for the records remaining reachable for after-the-fact investigation.

application_contribution: Splunk carries the whole detect-and-send path itself: a scheduled saved search that mails the SA and ISSO when account-disabling events are received, with the relay and sender for the email action held in alert_actions.conf.
citation: Two of the reviewed conditions fail configurations the benchmark accepts. savedsearches.conf alert_condition defaults to an empty string (savedsearches.conf.spec:270-274) and is only one of the ways a saved search triggers; counttype defaults to "always" and is used with relation and quantity instead (savedsearches.conf.spec:249-253), so alert_condition non_empty reports a finding against a working alert, and against a plain scheduled report, which is exactly what the product STIG check asks for (SPLK-CL-000020: "verify that a report exists to notify the SA and ISSO"). alert_actions.conf [email] subject defaults to "Splunk Alert: $name$" (alert_actions.conf.spec:199-201), so requiring it present tests a cosmetic field whose default is already populated and whose absence weakens nothing. What survives is the send path the fix text names: Splunk ships no mail server of its own ("You must have a Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) server available to send email. This is not included with the Splunk instance", alert_actions.conf.spec:276-285, default localhost), from defaults to the bare word "splunk" (alert_actions.conf.spec:163-165), action.email defaults to false (savedsearches.conf.spec:300-302), action.email.to is documented REQUIRED and is not defaulted in alert_actions.conf (savedsearches.conf.spec:304-306), and enableSched accepts only 0 or 1 with 0 the default (savedsearches.conf.spec:73-77). application_contribution: Splunk terminates sessions on its own timer: web.conf tools.sessions.timeout expires the Splunk Web session after a set period of inactivity, and ui_inactivity_timeout must not be set below 1, which would stop the browser-side pollers ever yielding and keep the session alive indefinitely.
citation: Three of the reviewed conditions fail a configuration built exactly as the benchmark authority prescribes. The product STIG fix for SPLK-CL-000010 sets one key, tools.session.timeout = 15, and its check makes a finding only where tools.sessions.timeout is missing or 16 or more. ui_inactivity_timeout max 15 appears in no check or fix text for that key, and its documented default is 60 (web.conf.spec:403-410), so the condition reports a finding against an instance configured per the fix text verbatim, which is a false finding of the most damaging kind. ui_inactivity_timeout present fails for the same reason: the default of 60 is at or above 1 and does not defeat termination, so demanding the key be declared penalizes a compliant default. server.conf [general] sessionTimeout present is also dropped here: the setting defaults to "1" (1 hour) and therefore already terminates the splunkd session (server.conf.spec:73-78), so requiring its declaration again fails the STIG-prescribed configuration; the eight-hour bound on that key is tested where the check text supplies a number, in SRG-APP-000295-WSR-000012. What is kept is grounded and directional: max 15 matches the product STIG check ("16 or more" is a finding), min 2 is the specification's own floor ("Use a value of 2 or higher, as a value of 1 causes a race condition with the browser refresh", web.conf.spec:924-932), and ui_inactivity_timeout min 1 catches the one value a site can set that defeats the requirement outright, since below 1 "Sessions stay alive for as long as the browser is open" (web.conf.spec:403-410); an absent key resolves to the documented default of 60 and satisfies it.

finding_statement: Splunk Web does not expire inactive sessions within the required period: web.conf [settings] tools.sessions.timeout is unset or 16 or more minutes, or ui_inactivity_timeout is set below 1, which stops the inactivity notification firing and keeps sessions alive for as long as the browser stays open.

application_contribution: Splunk bounds the life of a session from its own configuration: server.conf sessionTimeout caps the splunkd session and web.conf tools.sessions.timeout caps the Splunk Web session, so the eight-hour ceiling the check text names is expressible without anything outside the product.
citation: tools.sessions.restart_persist matches ^(0|false)$ is removed as invention. The setting governs only whether the session cookie survives the browser quitting, and the specification states persistence holds only "assuming the 'tools.sessions.timeout' has not been reached" (web.conf.spec:934-941), so it cannot extend a session past the timeout and does not decide an absolute ceiling. It defaults to true, appears in neither the SRG check text ("close sessions after eight hours or less") nor the product STIG fix text (which sets tools.session.timeout alone), so requiring false reports a finding against compliant systems over a setting that is not the control. The sessionTimeout regex is kept: it is directionally correct against sessionTimeout = <nonnegative integer>[s|m|h|d] with default "1" (1 hour) (server.conf.spec:73-78), admitting 1-8 bare or with h, 1-480m and 1-28800s, all of which are eight hours or less, and rejecting every d-suffixed value, each of which exceeds it. Where the key is absent the documented 1-hour default satisfies the bound. tools.sessions.timeout keeps the product STIG's max of 15 and gains the specification's own floor of 2 (web.conf.spec:929-930), which is the same key the authority's fix text sets.

application_contribution: Splunk closes an idle session from its own settings: web.conf tools.sessions.timeout is the inactivity period after which the Splunk Web session expires, and ui_inactivity_timeout must not be set below 1, which would stop the inactivity notification firing at all.
citation: ui_inactivity_timeout max 15 and ui_inactivity_timeout present are removed. The number 15 is the product STIG's value for a different key - the fix for SPLK-CL-000010 sets tools.session.timeout = 15 and touches nothing else - while ui_inactivity_timeout's documented default is 60 (web.conf.spec:403-410), so a max of 15 on that key reports a finding against an instance configured exactly as the benchmark authority prescribes, and present penalizes a default that does not defeat the requirement. The check text's own numbers (5, 10 and 20 minutes by application risk tier) are a bound on the idle close time, not on this notification interval, so transplanting any of them to ui_inactivity_timeout would be the same error with better provenance. min 1 is kept because it is the one setting of this key that defeats the requirement outright: below 1 "Sessions stay alive for as long as the browser is open" (web.conf.spec:408-409). tools.sessions.timeout keeps present and max 15 from the product STIG check ("missing or ... 16 or more"), which is inside even the strictest 5-minute tier's parent requirement, plus the specification's floor of 2 (web.conf.spec:929-930).

application_contribution: Splunk Web provides a logout control in its own interface for every authenticated session and no configuration setting removes it, so the application already carries this requirement as far as the product allows.
citation: Each of the five reviewed conditions produces a false finding. server.conf [general] invalidateSessionTokensOnLogout "has an effect only if search head clustering and App Key Value store are enabled" and defaults to false (server.conf.spec:81-87), so requiring it true fails a standalone indexer or search head where the setting does nothing at all. logoutCacheRefreshInterval "has no effect when 'invalidateSessionTokensOnLogout' is disabled" and defaults to 30s (server.conf.spec:89-92), so requiring it present tests nothing and can only fail an instance that has no reason to declare it. The three authentication.conf conditions sit in a [<saml-authSettings-key>] stanza that exists only where authType is SAML, against a default authType of Splunk (authentication.conf.spec:30-33, 44), and because conditions are ANDed they report a finding on every instance not using SAML; idpSLOUrl and redirectAfterLogoutToUrl have no defaults (authentication.conf.spec:687-690, 780-784), and sloBinding's "Acceptable options are 'HTTPPost' and 'HTTPRedirect'" with HTTPPost the default (authentication.conf.spec:1109-1113) means in:HTTPPost|HTTPRedirect cannot fail any legal value and decides nothing. Since no setting governs whether the logout capability exists, this is case 4: there is nothing to test, and the single-logout and cluster-token behavior belongs in external dependencies where it is stated rather than silently asserted.
external_dependencies: Where authentication is delegated to a SAML identity provider, the identity provider must publish and honor a single-logout endpoint at the configured idpSLOUrl and binding; Splunk can send the logout request but cannot make the identity provider end its own session.

Invalidating session tokens cluster-wide on logout requires search head clustering and the App Key Value store to be enabled, which is deployment architecture rather than a value assertable on a single instance.
Closing the browser or the remote-access session that carries it is the user's action and the hosting platform's, not the application's.
finding_statement: Not expected to be a finding against the application: Splunk Web presents a logout control for user-initiated sessions unconditionally, and an assessor records that observation; raise a finding only if a logout observed in the interface leaves the session usable.
manual_reason: No setting in the 10.4.2 specification set enables, disables or weakens the logout control; Splunk Web presents it unconditionally, so an assessor confirms the capability in the interface rather than reading a value.

application_contribution: Splunk Web renders its own logout page after a user-initiated logout; the application displays the message but exposes no setting that supplies, suppresses or alters its text.
citation: The reviewed criterion contradicts itself: its own contribution text states the logout page wording is compiled into the product and not exposed by configuration, then makes the verdict turn on authentication.conf redirectAfterLogoutToUrl. That setting has no default and lives inside a SAML [<saml-authSettings-key>] stanza (authentication.conf.spec:780-784) that exists only where authType is SAML against a default of Splunk (authentication.conf.spec:30-33), so as the single ANDed condition it reports a finding on every instance not using SAML - a finding for a message the product displays and no setting can change. The messages.conf keys the inventory carries for this requirement do not reach it either: [<component>:<key>] message, action and target define platform bulletin messages keyed to a component the software itself raises, with target choosing between Splunk Web and the log (messages.conf.spec:68-73, 79-83, 116-124), and there is no component or key for a user-initiated logout. Nothing in the specification set expresses the logout message, so the criterion is manual and redirectAfterLogoutToUrl is recorded as the related SAML behavior, not as a test.
external_dependencies: The wording of Splunk Web's built-in logout page is compiled into the product, so an assessor confirms the explicit logout message by observing a logout in the interface.
Where logout redirects to a SAML identity provider or to a URL named by redirectAfterLogoutToUrl, the final page the user sees is that service's and is outside the application.
Where the logout message must carry organization-specific wording, that is a product feature request, not a configuration item.
finding_statement: Not expected to be a finding against the application: Splunk Web displays its built-in logout page on a user-initiated logout, and an assessor records that observation; raise a finding only if no logout confirmation is displayed.
manual_reason: The wording of Splunk Web's logout page is compiled into the product and no .conf setting in the 10.4.2 specification set expresses it, so the explicit logout message is confirmed by observing a logout rather than by reading a value.

application_contribution: Splunk enforces the remote-access requirements the discussion names from its own configuration: HTTPS on Splunk Web instead of HTTP, and an access control list on each listener it owns in place of the default that accepts connections from anywhere.
citation: Four of the reviewed conditions have to go. authType not_equals Splunk and authSettings non_empty invert the check text, which makes a finding only where "the web server is not configured to enforce these requirements and an enterprise tool is not in place" - an either/or. The discussion's examples of the server enforcing the policy are "implementing IP filtering rules, using https instead of http for communication, implementing secure tokens, and validating users", and native Splunk authentication validates users, so forcing authType away from its documented default of Splunk (authentication.conf.spec:30-33) fails an instance that enforces the policy itself with TLS and ACLs. That is over-reach: delegated authentication is one way to satisfy the requirement, not a condition of it, and it belongs in external dependencies. The sslVersions pair is both out of scope for this requirement and unsatisfiable in a legal case: no TLS version appears in this check or fix text, and the regex requires the literal "tls1.2" although the specification states the version "tls" "selects all versions tls1.0 or newer" and "-" removes a version (web.conf.spec:239-248), so a compliant "tls,-tls1.0,-tls1.1" - tls1.2 only - is failed; TLS version floors are the subject of the crypto requirements, not AC-17(1). requireClientCert present demands a key whose default is false and which the check text never asks for (web.conf.spec:151-161). What remains is the application's full share: HTTPS exactly as the product STIG's own fix writes it under SPLK-CL-000290 (enableSplunkWebSSL = 1, privKeyPath, serverCert) and the IP filtering the discussion names, where acceptFrom defaults to "*" - "accept from anywhere" - on both of the listeners the application owns (web.conf.spec:1080-1096).

application_contribution: Splunk holds a network access control list on every listener it owns - web.conf acceptFrom for Splunk Web, server.conf [httpServer] acceptFrom for the management interface, and acceptFrom on the receiving input stanza - each of which defaults to accepting connections from anywhere until the organization's rules are written into it.
citation: Only the inputs.conf stanza changes, and it has to. acceptFrom is not a global inputs.conf setting: the specification defines it per input stanza, and the receiving stanza the product STIG's own fix configures is [splunktcp-ssl:<port>] (SPLK-CL-000290; inputs.conf.spec:876, 908-910, with the rule syntax and "Default: * (accept from anywhere)" at 577-591). A condition attached to an empty stanza name cannot be looked up in any file, so it would report a finding for a key that was never read - a confident status that is not evidence. The not_equals "*" direction is correct on all three listeners: "*" is the documented default and "matches anything", while a real restriction such as "!192.0.2/24, *" is not equal to "*" and passes, which is the behavior the specification's own example describes (web.conf.spec:1090-1096, inputs.conf.spec:587-591).

application_contribution: Splunk owns several levers for an immediate disconnect - startwebserver 0 or httpport 0 stops the Splunk Web listener, disabled on an input stanza stops a receiver, and a "!" deny rule in acceptFrom blocks a source on any listener - and all of them are available whether or not a site has declared the keys.
citation: Every condition in the reviewed criterion is a present test on a key whose absence is normal and whose presence proves nothing. The check makes a finding only where "the web server is not capable of or cannot be configured to disconnect or disable remote access", and the capability exists in the product regardless: startwebserver defaults to 1 with "0 disables Splunk Web" (web.conf.spec:23-26), httpport defaults to 8000 and "If omitted or 0 the server will NOT start an http listener" (web.conf.spec:28-33), and acceptFrom defaults to "*" while accepting a "!" prefix "to cause the rule to reject the connection" (web.conf.spec:1080-1096). Requiring those keys present reports a finding against an instance that is fully capable of the disconnect, which is over-reach of the worst kind because the thing demanded has no bearing on the thing checked; worse, requiring startwebserver or httpport to be declared tells an assessor nothing about whether an administrator can act. The inputs.conf disabled condition carries an empty stanza name and cannot be evaluated at all. The two acceptFrom non_empty conditions duplicate SRG-APP-000315-WSR-000004, where the check text actually asks for a restriction. No value decides this requirement, so it is a manual confirmation.
external_dependencies: The administrator's authority and the organizational procedure for ordering and executing an immediate disconnect sit outside the application.
The check also requires that the disconnect methods be documented so the right action is taken during an attack; that is a document, not a setting.
Network-level isolation of the instance during an attack is carried by the hosting network, and host-level service control by the operating system.
finding_statement: Not expected to be a finding against the application: Splunk can stop its web listener, disable an individual input, or reject a source with a deny rule, and an assessor confirms these methods are documented; raise a finding only where the documented procedure does not exist.
manual_reason: The requirement is a capability, and the capability is present in the product whichever way the keys are left; no value decides it, so an assessor confirms the methods and their documentation rather than reading a setting.

application_contribution: Splunk both identifies and authenticates the source of transferred data from its own configuration: connection_host stamps each received event with the sending system's address or resolved name, TLS with a required client certificate authenticates the sender on the receiving port, the forwarder presents its own certificate and validates the receiver, Splunk Web serves over HTTPS, and no UDP input is accepted because a UDP input has no connection to authenticate.
citation: Three corrections. First, serverCert, sslPassword and requireClientCert are moved to the [SSL] stanza. They are legal inside [splunktcp-ssl:<port>] only as per-port deviations - "To specify global TLS settings, that are applicable for all ports, add the settings to the [SSL] stanza. Specify any TLS setting that deviates from the global setting here" (inputs.conf.spec:919-932) - and the product STIG's own fix for SPLK-CL-000290 writes [splunktcp-ssl:9997] with disabled = 0 and then puts serverCert and sslPassword under [SSL]. Requiring them under the port stanza therefore reports a finding against an instance built exactly as the benchmark authority prescribes, and against every deployment that sets TLS once for all ports; [SSL] is also the stanza whose values apply to all receiving ports (inputs.conf.spec:986-1015). Second, inputs.conf host non_empty is removed because it asks for the opposite of the requirement: connection_host = none "leaves the host as specified in inputs.conf, typically the hostname of the system running Splunk software" (inputs.conf.spec:526-534), so a static host is how source identity is lost, not retained, and requiring it alongside connection_host in ip|dns demands both halves of a contradiction - it also carried an empty stanza name and could not be evaluated. Third, the UDP rule was missing. SPLK-CL-000270 shares this SRG and is checked as "If any input is configured to use a UDP port, this is a finding" and fixed by replacing UDP inputs with TCP ports; a datagram input authenticates nothing, so this is the most direct application-layer condition the requirement has, and it is machine-checkable against both UDP stanza forms (inputs.conf.spec:1227, 1314). requireClientCert true is kept deliberately: server-side TLS authenticates the receiver, not the source, and the fix text's own clientCert on the forwarder authenticates the sender only if the receiver demands the certificate (inputs.conf.spec:1015-1023). connection_host in:ip|dns is within the setting's vocabulary [ip|dns|none] and both receiving defaults are already ip or dns (inputs.conf.spec:526-534, 889-891), so it fails only an explicit "none".
