application_contribution: Splunk decides which ports it opens and what protocol each one speaks: it can be configured with no connectionless input at all, and it can require TLS on the management port, the web port, and the receiving port with a declared protocol version list and cipher suite.
citation: SPLK-CL-000270 and SPLK-CL-000290 check and fix text; inputs.conf.spec:1314 ([udp:<port>]), server.conf.spec:724 (enableSplunkdSSL), web.conf.spec:70 (enableSplunkWebSSL, default false), server.conf.spec:765 and 775 (sslVersions, default varies by shipped file), server.conf.spec:940 (cipherSuite, otherwise the OpenSSL default)

conditions.rationale: The specification states that a value of false means the daemon runs TLS on no port, which would leave the management and KV Store ports nonsecure; the setting is a boolean, so either spelling of true satisfies it.
The product STIG check requires that enableSplunkWebSSL be set, and its fix text sets it to 1; the specification defines it as a boolean that toggles between HTTP and HTTPS, with a default of false.
The collection probes stanza existence with the key "*", so this tests that no udp:<port> input stanza exists. The bare [udp] settings stanza is not probed that way and is excluded.
server.conf sslConfig sslVersions is a comma-separated list, so the whole value must consist only of tls1.2 and tls1.3 for no deprecated version to be offered.

external_dependencies: Which ports are reachable from where, carried by the host firewall and the network; the application can close a listener but cannot filter who reaches an open one.
The protocol versions and ciphers the underlying TLS library actually offers, carried by the platform build, since the shipped cipher default comes from the OpenSSL binary.
Approval of the ports and protocols in use for a production system, which is an organizational determination recorded against the ports, protocols, and services registration.
finding_statement: A UDP input remains configured, or a management, web, or receiving listener does not require TLS with a declared version list and cipher suite, so the application still offers a nonsecure or unnecessary port or protocol.

application_contribution: On a network input Splunk stamps each received event with the identity of the connection it arrived on, and the application can keep that behavior rather than discarding it.
citation: Central Log Server SRG SRG-APP-000516-AU-000330 check text; SPLK-CL-000260 check and fix text; inputs.conf.spec:526 (connection_host = [ip|dns|none]), inputs.conf.spec:60 (host), transforms.conf.spec:241 (DEST_KEY)

conditions.rationale: The check requires that each aggregated record include the identity of the original source host or device. The specification gives this setting the vocabulary ip, dns, or none; ip and dns both record the sending device, while none discards the connection's identity. The check inventory captured this vocabulary in place of the stanza name for this requirement, which identifies it as the mechanism determined for it.

external_dependencies: Whether each sending device puts its own identity in the payload, and whether the name service resolves the sending address, carried by the forwarders and by the network name service.

Where the true origin is inside the message rather than on the connection - a relayed syslog record, for example - the product STIG fix directs a props.conf and transforms.conf host extraction instead; which extraction is correct depends on the format each sending device emits, so it is a per-source data decision (SPLK-CL-000260 fix text, transforms.conf.spec:241).
finding_statement: A network input is set to discard the connection's host identity, so records aggregated through it do not retain the device where the event occurred.

application_contribution: Splunk chooses which transports it will accept log records on, and it can be configured with no connectionless receiver, leaving only its acknowledged TCP receivers in service.
citation: SPLK-CL-000270 check and fix text; Central Log Server SRG SRG-APP-000516-AU-000340 check text; inputs.conf.spec:1314 ([udp:<port>]), inputs.conf.spec:1227 ([udp://<remote server>:<port>]), outputs.conf.spec:121 ([tcpout:<target_group>])

conditions.rationale: The collection probes stanza existence with the key "*", so this tests that no udp:<port> input stanza exists. The bare [udp] settings stanza is not probed that way and is excluded.

external_dependencies: The transport each sending device actually uses, carried by that device's own configuration - on a Splunk forwarder, its outputs.conf [tcpout:<target_group>] (outputs.conf.spec:121) - since a receiver can refuse connectionless traffic but cannot make a sender switch.
Network reachability of the TCP receiving port, carried by the firewall and the network.
finding_statement: A UDP input remains configured on the aggregating instance, so the application still accepts log records over a transport that does not acknowledge delivery.

application_contribution: Splunk can run a detection search on a schedule and send its result to named recipients by email, so the notification path and the people on it are expressed in the application's own configuration.
citation: Central Log Server SRG SRG-APP-000516-AU-000350 check text; SPLK-CL-000280 check and fix text; savedsearches.conf.spec:73 (enableSched = [0 | 1], default 0), savedsearches.conf.spec:79 (cron_schedule), savedsearches.conf.spec:300 (action.email, default false), savedsearches.conf.spec:304 (action.email.to, REQUIRED), alert_actions.conf.spec:276 (mailserver)

conditions.rationale: The check requires that the server be configured to notify, which means a search that runs by itself rather than on demand. The specification states that 0 and 1 are the only acceptable values and that 1 runs the search on a schedule.
The specification defines this as the cron expression that runs the search; a scheduled search with no schedule never fires, so the detection would never notify.
The specification defines action.email as the boolean that enables the email action for a search, with a default of false, so it must be on for the search to notify anyone.

The specification marks this setting REQUIRED and defines it as the comma-delimited recipient list. The requirement names the SA and ISSO at a minimum but leaves their addresses to the organization, so the criterion is that the product expresses a recipient list, not which addresses it holds.
The specification defines this as the mail transfer agent the email action sends through; without it the configured notification cannot leave the instance.

external_dependencies: Who the SA and ISSO are and what detection logic constitutes an attack across multiple devices, both organization-defined; the product STIG verifies this part by interviewing the SA and confirming receipt with the ISSO rather than by reading configuration (SPLK-CL-000280 check text).
Delivery of the message, carried by the mail transfer agent and the network.
Where analysis is performed by another device, the benchmark marks the requirement not applicable, which is a deployment-design determination.
finding_statement: No scheduled search carries an enabled email action with a recipient list and a reachable mail server, so the application cannot notify anyone when a detection fires across multiple hosts.

application_contribution: Splunk can hand a triggered detection to an outside system as it fires, through the webhook alert action or a script action, which is how a ticket is opened from the application without a person in the loop.
citation: Central Log Server SRG SRG-APP-000516-AU-000360 check text; alert_actions.conf.spec:599 ([webhook]), alert_actions.conf.spec:87 (command), alert_actions.conf.spec:100 (payload_format = [xml|json], default xml), savedsearches.conf.spec:73 (enableSched), savedsearches.conf.spec:403 (action.script)

conditions.rationale: The check requires that tickets be created automatically as events are detected. The specification defines command as the search command or pipeline that executes an alert action, so the webhook action must carry one for the application to be able to post a triggered detection to a ticket system.

The requirement asks for detection in real time. The specification permits only 0 and 1 here and states that 1 runs the search on a schedule, which is what makes the action fire without a person running the search.

external_dependencies: The ticket system itself and the endpoint it accepts submissions on, which the application posts to but does not provide.
Which threats and events of interest warrant a ticket, left to the organization by the check text.
Detection "within seconds" depends on a real-time or continuously scheduled search and the search capacity to sustain it, which is a sizing and deployment-design decision rather than a setting.
Where the server performs no analysis, the benchmark marks the requirement not applicable, which is a deployment-design determination.
finding_statement: No alert action is configured that can hand a triggered detection to an outside system, or detections are not scheduled to run by themselves, so the application cannot open a ticket as an event of interest is detected.

application_contribution: Splunk can bring account-action events from every device in scope together by routing each input's data to a declared index and classifying the events with event types, so a single search reaches all of them.
citation: Central Log Server SRG SRG-APP-000516-AU-000370 check text; inputs.conf.spec:93 (index), inputs.conf.spec:128 (queue = [parsingQueue|indexQueue]), eventtypes.conf.spec:36 ([<$EVENTTYPE>]), eventtypes.conf.spec:51 (search)

conditions.rationale: The specification defines an event type stanza by the search that selects its events, which is how account-action events from differently formatted sources are given one name and aggregated in a single query.

external_dependencies: Which events each sending device emits for account creation, modification, disablement, and removal, carried by that device's own audit policy; the application can only aggregate what it is sent.

A props.conf or transforms.conf route that discards events to the null queue would drop them before indexing; whether a given filter does so is a per-deployment data-routing decision (props.conf.spec:1043, transforms.conf.spec:241).
Which account-action events are collected for each in-scope device, which is not decidable from inputs.conf because the scope of coverage is organization-defined.
finding_statement: Inputs do not declare the index their data lands in, or no event type classifies account actions, so the application does not bring account-action events together for the devices within its scope of coverage.

application_contribution: Splunk can carry a severity value on each alert it raises, so the organization's own criticality levels are expressed in the application's configuration rather than assigned by hand after the fact.
citation: Central Log Server SRG SRG-APP-000516-AU-000380 check text; savedsearches.conf.spec:887 (alert.severity = <integer>, valid values 1 through 6, default 3); props.conf.spec:80 ([<spec>] stanza forms)

conditions.rationale: The check reads the site's system security plan for the criticality levels in use and then looks for them in the configuration. The specification gives this setting the levels 1 through 6, so the criterion is that the product expresses a severity for its alerts; the organization's own assignment of level to event is not something to invent here.

external_dependencies: The criticality levels themselves and the mapping of event to level, which the check takes from the site's system security plan.
Severity or facility values that each sending device stamps on its own records before transmission, carried by that device.
finding_statement: Alerts carry no severity value, so the application does not express the organization's criticality levels for the events it receives from individual devices and hosts.

application_contribution: Splunk can require TLS on every path through which its analysis, viewing, and indexing functions are reached - the web interface, the management port, and the receiving port - with a configured server certificate, private key, and trust anchor, and it governs access to those functions through declared roles.
citation: SPLK-CL-000290 check and fix text; web.conf.spec:70 (enableSplunkWebSSL, default false), web.conf.spec:82 (serverCert), web.conf.spec:75 (privKeyPath), server.conf.spec:724 (enableSplunkdSSL), server.conf.spec:996 (sslRootCAPath), inputs.conf.spec:986 ([SSL]), inputs.conf.spec:990 (serverCert), inputs.conf.spec:1015 (requireClientCert), authorize.conf.spec:67 ([role_<roleName>]), authorize.conf.spec:79 (importRoles)

conditions.rationale: The product STIG check requires that enableSplunkWebSSL be set and its fix text sets it to 1; this is the path by which analysis and viewing functions are reached. The specification defines it as a boolean with a default of false.

The product STIG fix text sets privKeyPath to the key generated for that certificate; the specification notes the setting otherwise falls back to the automatically generated key under the installation's auth directory, which is not an approved certificate.
The specification states that false means the daemon runs TLS on no port, which would leave the indexing and management path unprotected.

The product STIG fix text configures the indexer's receiving port under [splunktcp-ssl] with an [SSL] serverCert, which is the trusted path for the indexing function; the specification states the certificate must be in PEM format and has no default.
A trusted path requires an anchor to validate against; the specification defines this as the concatenated certificate authority store the instance trusts.
The product STIG fix text sets serverCert to the approved certificate in PEM format; without it the enabled TLS listener has no identity for a client to validate.
The product STIG fix text sets serverCert to the approved certificate in PEM format; without it the enabled TLS listener has no identity for a client to validate.

external_dependencies: The certificates themselves and their issuance by a certificate authority the organization approves, carried by the public key infrastructure; the product STIG fix text names an approved certificate without the application being able to judge one.
The trusted path from the analyst's workstation to the instance, carried by the network and by the workstation's own trust store.
Whether every sending device presents a certificate, which the product STIG verifies by reading the receiver's connection metrics rather than from configuration (SPLK-CL-000290 check text).
finding_statement: The web interface, the management port, or the receiving port does not require TLS with a configured certificate, private key, and trust anchor, so the analysis, viewing, and indexing functions are reachable over a path the application does not protect.

application_contribution: Splunk can show that no seeded installation password remains in its configuration, and it can declare a password policy and force any account whose password falls short of it to change that password at next login.
citation: Web Server SRG SRG-APP-000516-WSR-000079 check and fix text; user-seed.conf.spec:14 and 32 (PASSWORD, clear text), user-seed.conf.spec:36 (HASHED_PASSWORD), authentication.conf.spec:509 (forceWeakPasswordChange), authentication.conf.spec:441 (minPasswordLength), authentication.conf.spec:514 (lockoutUsers)

conditions.rationale: The check makes an account that still holds no password or a default password a finding. user-seed.conf is where the installation's initial password is supplied, and the specification notes the clear-text form is the less secure option, so a PASSWORD still declared there is an installed default left in the configuration.

The fix text directs that passwords still at their default be changed. This is the setting that compels a change at next login for any account whose password does not satisfy the configured policy, which is how the application reaches accounts an assessor cannot enumerate from a file.

external_dependencies: Whether each existing account's password has actually been changed from its installed value, which is held in the instance's user store rather than in a .conf file an assessor can read.
Operating system accounts created by the installation package, carried by the operating system.
Accounts held in the directory service where authentication is external, carried by that service's own password policy.
finding_statement: A seed password remains declared in the configuration, or no password policy is declared and accounts with weak passwords are not forced to change them, so the application does not require installed accounts to hold a changed, non-default password.

application_contribution: The application can hold the two concrete settings the benchmark authority states for this product, and can carry the rest of the applicable guidance as explicit values in its own .conf files rather than relying on shipped defaults.
citation: SPLK-CL-000290 check and fix text; Web Server SRG SRG-APP-000516-WSR-000174 check text; web.conf.spec:70 (enableSplunkWebSSL, default false), server.conf.spec:724 (enableSplunkdSSL)

conditions.rationale: This is one of only two concrete values the product STIG states for this product, and its check text requires that enableSplunkWebSSL be set; the specification defines it as a boolean with a default of false, so the configured guidance is observable here.

The product STIG fix text configures TLS on the receiving and management paths; the specification states that false runs TLS on no port, so this is the setting that carries that direction in the daemon's configuration.

external_dependencies: The rest of this requirement is the sum of the other rules in this checklist: it has no setting of its own beyond the values the product STIG states, and the check inventory attaches whole .conf files to it rather than a key.

Which guidance applies - the STIGs, NSA configuration guides, CTOs, and DTMs in scope - is an organizational determination, and the operating system, network, and procedural portions of those documents are carried outside the application.
Precedence matters when reading the result: a value in the system-local layer outranks the hardening app, so guidance delivered as an app can be overridden on the host.
finding_statement: The settings the benchmark authority states for this product are not configured, so the application is not configured in accordance with the security configuration guidance that applies to it.

application_contribution: Splunk records its own enforcement actions in two places it controls: the configuration change log, which captures every change to a .conf file including the values that changed, and the audit trail, which it can queue to an index so the records are searchable and retained.
citation: Central Log Server SRG SRG-APP-000805-AU-000240 check and fix text; server.conf.spec:599 (config_change_tracker disabled, default false), server.conf.spec:608 (mode = [auto|diff|track-only], default auto), server.conf.spec:636 (denylist, no default), server.conf.spec:641 (log_throttling_disabled, default true), server.conf.spec:661 (exclude_fields), audit.conf.spec:24 (queueing, default true)

conditions.rationale: The specification states that false means configuration changes are captured in the configuration change log and true means they are not, so false is the only value under which the application generates these records at all.

Of the three permitted values, the specification states that auto and diff log all changes including the setting values, while track-only logs that a file changed but excludes the values. A record that omits what was enforced does not satisfy the requirement; the specification also notes auto keeps the instance on the latest feature set.

The specification states that true sends audit events to the index queue, and that with false an inputs.conf stanza must be added to tail the audit log for the events to reach an index. Automatic generation into the searchable record is the application's share.

The specification defines this as a regular expression whose matching paths are not monitored for configuration change tracking, so any value narrows the record below what the requirement asks for; the setting has no default.
The specification defines this as stanza keys to omit when writing a configuration change, so any value removes part of the enforcement action from the record.

The specification states that true logs each change individually as it is detected, while false coalesces changes made within the throttling window into a single event, which loses the individual enforcement actions; the default is true.

external_dependencies: Enforcement actions taken outside the application - operating system access control decisions, firewall denials, directory service lockouts - carried by those components and recorded by them.
Retention, protection, and off-host copy of the records once written, which the AU family assesses rather than this requirement.
Individual change logging requires a Linux host with the inotify file system event interface, which is a platform property.
finding_statement: Configuration change tracking is switched off, set to track-only, narrowed by a denylist or excluded fields, or the audit trail is not queued to an index, so the application does not automatically generate a complete record of its own enforcement actions.

application_contribution: Splunk writes a record of every change made to its own configuration files, including the values that changed, and queues its audit trail to an index; it also holds the capability that permits audit settings to be altered, so the record cannot be quietly narrowed by an ordinary user.
citation: Web Server SRG SRG-APP-000805-WSR-000140 check and fix text; server.conf.spec:599 (disabled, default false), server.conf.spec:608 (mode, default auto), server.conf.spec:636 (denylist), server.conf.spec:661 (exclude_fields), audit.conf.spec:24 (queueing, default true), authorize.conf.spec:483 ([capability::change_audit])

conditions.rationale: The specification states that false captures configuration changes in the change log and true does not, so false is the only value under which the server generates records of the changes it enforces.

The specification states that auto and diff log all changes including setting values, while track-only excludes the values; a record that does not say what was changed does not evidence the enforcement action.
The specification states that true sends audit events to the index queue and that false requires a separate input to tail the audit log, so true is what makes generation automatic.
Any regular expression here removes the matching paths from change tracking, narrowing the record of enforcement actions; the setting has no default.
Any value here omits named stanza keys from the written record, so part of the enforcement action is lost.

external_dependencies: Enforcement actions by components in front of the web interface - a reverse proxy's denials, for example - carried by that component.
Operating system level access denials against the installation's files, carried by the operating system's own audit subsystem.
Which roles hold the change_audit capability that permits audit settings to be altered is assessed under the role requirement, SRG-APP-000380-WSR-000072 (authorize.conf.spec:483).
finding_statement: Configuration change tracking is switched off, set to track-only, or narrowed by a denylist or excluded fields, or the audit trail is not queued to an index, so the web server does not automatically generate records of the enforcement actions it takes.

application_contribution: Splunk can close the channel by which an app is pulled straight onto the instance, confine the capability that permits an app to be installed to administrative roles, and verify after the fact that the installed files still match the release manifest.
citation: Central Log Server SRG SRG-APP-000810-AU-000250 check and fix text; server.conf.spec:1734 (allowInternetAccess), authorize.conf.spec:760 ([capability::install_apps]), authorize.conf.spec:68 (capabilities disabled by default), limits.conf.spec:4450 (installed_files_integrity = enabled | log_only | disabled, default enabled)

conditions.rationale: The requirement is to prevent installation without verification. This setting is what lets the instance reach the remote applications repository and install from it directly, bypassing any acceptance step; the specification defines it as a boolean, so either spelling of false closes the channel.

The specification states that "enabled" is the only accepted value for a capability because capabilities are disabled by default, so absence from a non-administrative role stanza is the configured denial of the ability to install a component.

Where the product cannot verify a signature before load, the nearest capability it has is detecting that the installed set no longer matches the release manifest. Of the three permitted values, only "enabled" both posts the detected problem and logs it.

external_dependencies: Verification that a component is digitally signed with a certificate the organization recognizes: Splunk Enterprise 10.4.2 exposes no setting that requires or validates a package signature before an app loads, so this part of the objective is carried by the package producer's signing, the organization's software acceptance procedure, and the operating system package manager's signature checking.
Which software and firmware components are in scope, which the requirement leaves to the organization.
Firmware components, which are outside the application entirely and are carried by the platform.
finding_statement: The instance can reach the remote applications repository, a non-administrative role holds the capability to install apps, or installed-file integrity verification is off, so the application does not confine component installation to the paths where a verification step can be applied.

application_contribution: Splunk can compute and store rawdata-slice hashes for every index (enableDataIntegrityControl), so later alteration of indexed records is detectable.
citation: INVENTION. Removed authorize.conf [role_<roleName>] delete_by_keyword absent: it cannot be satisfied. authorize.conf.spec gives a role capability as "<capability> = <enabled>" and notes "'enabled' is the only accepted value here, as capabilities are disabled by default", so a role stanza cannot express a denial; and the product ships [role_can_delete] with delete_by_keyword = enabled in system/default/authorize.conf, which assess.sh reads through btool's merged view. The condition therefore fails every stock installation. Restricting delete is real, but it is enforced by not placing anyone in that role, which authorize.conf does not record, so it moves to external_dependencies. The retained condition is the one the benchmark authority actually specifies.

conditions.rationale: SPLK-CL-000090 fix text: "enableDataIntegrityControl = 1 or True" under each index; its check text makes it a finding where the setting is missing or set to 0 or false.

external_dependencies: Filesystem permissions on the index rawdata and hash files - the operating system, not Splunk, prevents direct tampering with bucket contents on disk.
Membership of the delete-capable role, and therefore who can actually remove indexed records, is account provisioning and directory administration, not a Splunk setting.
finding_statement: enableDataIntegrityControl is not set to 1 or true for the indexes in scope, so Splunk does not compute or store the rawdata hashes needed to detect later alteration of the records it received.

application_contribution: Splunk can declare the receiving input that accepts records from the covered hosts and devices, a Splunk-to-Splunk receiver for forwarded data.
citation: INVENTION. The original condition named key "splunktcp" inside stanza [splunktcp]. inputs.conf has no setting of that name - splunktcp is a stanza, not a key - so the engine searches [splunktcp] for a key that cannot exist and reports it absent on every instance, a guaranteed false finding. The determined row carries an empty key, which assess.sh treats as a stanza-presence test, so key is set to empty to match that convention. Scope caveat for the assessor: where the covered hosts send by HEC or syslog instead, the corresponding input stanza carries this objective and the receiver named here would not apply.

conditions.rationale: SPLK-CL-000110 fix text: "On the indexer, configure the inputs.conf file with the information of the forwarders that are sending the data for analysis"; the determined row for this requirement is a stanza-presence test with no key.

external_dependencies: The list of in-scope devices and hosts is organization-defined and held in the site security plan; SPLK-CL-000100 directs the assessor to that document to decide whether the declared inputs cover it.
Each sending host's own forwarding configuration (outputs.conf on the forwarder, or the device's syslog target) is configured on that host, not on the instance under review.
finding_statement: No Splunk-to-Splunk receiving input is declared in inputs.conf, so the instance has no configured means of accepting the log records forwarded from the hosts and devices in its scope of coverage.

application_contribution: Splunk ships no NTP client, so it cannot synchronize a clock; what it configures is faithful timestamp recognition on the records it receives, plus the skew bounds it tolerates between a search head and its peers.
citation: Under-test corrected. The original excluded only NONE. props.conf.spec treats the two values together - "Both 'CURRENT' and 'NONE' explicitly disable the per-text timestamp identification" - and CURRENT is the worse case for this requirement, since it substitutes the aggregator's clock for the time the record carries, which is exactly the agreement the requirement is about. SRG-APP-000096-AU-000690 in this same group already excludes both, so leaving CURRENT permitted here made two criteria resting on one setting disagree. The skew conditions are kept: both are ceilings and the direction is correct.

conditions.rationale: props.conf.spec: "Both 'CURRENT' and 'NONE' explicitly disable the per-text timestamp identification"; CURRENT "sets the time of the event to the time that the event was merged from lines", which is the log server's own clock rather than the time the record carries.

limits.conf.spec: "Absolute value of the largest time skew, in seconds, that is tolerated between the native clock on the search head and the native clock on the peer... If this time skew is exceeded, a warning is logged. Default: 60." A ceiling, so the tolerance must not be relaxed past the product default.

limits.conf.spec: "Absolute value of the largest time skew, in seconds, that is allowed when configuring a search peer from a search head... If the difference in time (skew) between the search head and the peer is greater than 'addpeer_skew_limit', the search peer is not added. Default: 600."

external_dependencies: Clock synchronization to within one second of the host server, and to the same upstream time source as the covered hosts and devices, is performed by the operating system's time service; Splunk Enterprise 10.4.2 contains no NTP client for the check text's conditional clause to apply to.
finding_statement: Timestamp recognition is disabled for the sourcetypes in scope (DATETIME_CONFIG set to NONE or CURRENT), so the time recorded on a received record is the log server's own processing time rather than the time the record carries.

application_contribution: Where this instance is one of several log servers, Splunk can forward everything it receives to the central aggregation server: a [tcpout:<target_group>] stanza carries the aggregator's host and port in 'server', the top-level 'defaultGroup' selects that group so all data is sent, and indexAndForward keeps a local copy in addition on a heavy forwarder.
citation: SRG-APP-000086-AU-000390 check text; SPLK-CL-000110 check and fix text; outputs.conf.spec:61-70 ([tcpout], defaultGroup = <comma-separated list>); outputs.conf.spec:72-79 (indexAndForward = <boolean>, Default: false); outputs.conf.spec:118-130 ([tcpout:<target_group>], server = <comma-separated list>)

conditions.rationale: The spec states "The forwarder sends all data to the specified groups. If you don't want to forward data automatically, don't configure this setting" - a populated defaultGroup is therefore what makes onward forwarding active. SPLK-CL-000110 fix text: "configure the outputs.conf with the information of the indexer that the data will be sent to."

The spec defines server as the comma-separated list of systems to send data to over TCP, required unless indexerDiscovery is set; this is where the central aggregation server's host and port are named.

external_dependencies: Whether the enclave holds multiple log servers, and therefore whether this requirement applies at all, is read from the network architecture documentation. The application cannot determine its own place in the topology, and a single-log-server site is not a finding against it.
Existence and acceptance of the central aggregation server, SIEM or consolidated events repository, which is a separate system.
Transport protection for the forwarded records, configured in the outputs.conf SSL settings and assessed under the SC requirements.
finding_statement: Where this instance is one of multiple log servers, Splunk Enterprise has no outputs.conf target group naming the central aggregation server, or no defaultGroup selecting it, so the records it receives are not forwarded to the consolidated repository.

application_contribution: Splunk retains the raw record verbatim and stamps index-time attributes on it: the destination index and sourcetype assigned per data input, and the event time derived by the timestamp extractor.
citation: INVENTION. Removed field_filters.conf [<fieldFilterName>] action not_in "host"=null()|"source"=null()|"sourcetype"=null()|"_time"=null(). field_filters.conf.spec defines action as "<field> = <operator>" with "<operator> ::= null() | sha256() | sha512() | <string literal> | sed(<string literal>)", an open value space: sha256(), a replacement literal, or a sed expression on _raw removes or rewrites an attribute just as effectively, and any difference in quoting or spacing evades an exact-match list. The condition yields a confident pass that is not evidence. Field filters also act on search results, not on what the index retains. Stanza placeholders [<input stanza>] and [<spec>] were replaced with the empty stanza the determined rows carry, since assess.sh matches stanza names literally and a placeholder never matches. DATETIME_CONFIG aligned with SRG-APP-000096-AU-000690.

conditions.rationale: SPLK-CL-000130 fix text directs the attribute work to props.conf, whose stanzas are selected by the sourcetype assigned to each input, so a record with no sourcetype gets no attribute handling.
props.conf.spec: both NONE and CURRENT "explicitly disable the per-text timestamp identification", so the date and time attribute the record arrived with is not retained.

external_dependencies: The DoD/organization-defined attribute list is held in the site security plan; the check text defers to it, so the criterion tests only that Splunk assigns the attributes it controls.
Where field filters are defined, comparing the fields they mask against the organization's attribute list is an inspection against that document, not a condition configuration can decide.

Automatic aggregation of account-action events for every in-scope device, which is not decidable from inputs.conf because the scope of coverage is organization-defined; the application-layer share is the existence of a receiving listener.
finding_statement: Splunk does not stamp the index-time attributes it controls on the records in scope - a destination index, a sourcetype, or a recognized event time is missing - so the attributes the organization requires are not retained.

application_contribution: Splunk's web tier records system access in the Splunk Web HTTP access log named by web.conf log.access_file and REST access in splunkd_access.log for every endpoint not excluded by restmap.conf includeInAccessLog; authentication successes and failures and splunkd startup and shutdown are written by the product unconditionally, and the audit trail reaches a searchable index when audit.conf [auditTrail] queueing is true.
citation: SRG-APP-000089-WSR-000047 check text; web.conf.spec:16 ([settings]), web.conf.spec:871-874 (log.access_file = <filename>, Default: web_access.log); restmap.conf.spec:70 ([<rest endpoint name>:<endpoint description string>]), restmap.conf.spec:138-142 (includeInAccessLog = <boolean>, Default: true); audit.conf.spec:23-29 ([auditTrail], queueing = <boolean>, Default: true)

conditions.rationale: The check text requires system access to be logged; log.access_file is the HTTP access log filename, and leaving it empty leaves Splunk Web with no access log.

The spec states that when set to false requests do not appear in splunkd_access.log; excluding an endpoint removes system access records for it. Default is true, so an unmodified instance satisfies the condition.

The spec states that when set to false "you must add an inputs.conf stanza to tail the audit log for the events [to] reach your index"; with queueing true the authentication and access audit events are indexed as generated.

external_dependencies: System startup and shutdown records are written by splunkd to its own service log with no configuration surface, so that part of the objective is verified by inspecting the written log rather than by reading configuration.
The operating system's service manager decides when splunkd and Splunk Web start and stop, so the boundaries of a startup and shutdown record belong to it.

audit.conf in Splunk Enterprise 10.4.2 declares only 'queueing' under [auditTrail]; the 'logging_format' key carried in the check inventory is not a setting in this release's specification, so no condition is written over it and the audit record format is fixed in the product.
finding_statement: Splunk Enterprise has no web access log configured, excludes REST endpoints from splunkd_access.log, or sets audit.conf [auditTrail] queueing to false without an input tailing the audit log, so system access and authentication events are not recorded or indexed by the application.

application_contribution: Splunk can restrict who may change what is collected and retained: the capabilities that let a user alter audit settings, inputs, forwarding and index definitions (change_audit, edit_monitor, edit_tcp, edit_forwarders, indexes_edit) are granted per role in authorize.conf and are disabled unless listed, and authentication.conf [roleMap_<authSettings-key>] binds directory groups to those roles rather than to individual local accounts.
citation: SRG-APP-000090-AU-000070 check text; SPLK-CL-000140 check and fix text; authorize.conf.spec:67-77 ([role_<roleName>], <capability> = <enabled>, "'enabled' is the only accepted value here, as capabilities are disabled by default"); authorize.conf.spec:483-485 ([capability::change_audit]), :555 ([capability::edit_forwarders]), :597 ([capability::edit_monitor]), :699 ([capability::edit_tcp]), :753 ([capability::indexes_edit]); authentication.conf.spec:351-360 ([roleMap_<authSettings-key>])

conditions.rationale: The capability lets a user change audit settings through the audit endpoints and reload them, which is the selection of what is audited; the general-purpose 'user' role must not hold it. Capabilities are disabled unless listed, so an unmodified role satisfies the condition.
Editing index definitions changes which events are retained and for how long, so the general-purpose role must not hold it.
Editing monitor inputs changes which events are collected and therefore available to retain.
Editing TCP inputs changes which events are received from the covered hosts and devices.
Editing forwarder settings changes where received events are sent and whether they are retained here.

external_dependencies: The ISSM's list of individuals or roles appointed to select which auditable events are retained, and the comparison of role membership against it, is an organizational record; SPLK-CL-000140 performs that comparison against site documentation.

Membership of the LDAP or SAML group mapped to the privileged role is held in the directory service and administered outside the application, which is why SPLK-CL-000140 directs the assessor to the LDAP administrator for it.
finding_statement: The general-purpose 'user' role in authorize.conf holds one or more of the capabilities that select what is collected and retained (change_audit, indexes_edit, edit_monitor, edit_tcp, edit_forwarders), so accounts beyond those appointed by the ISSM can change which auditable events are retained.

application_contribution: Splunk's audit trail is generated by splunkd from the moment it starts and has no enable switch. What the application configures is whether those audit events are routed into the index queue as they are generated (audit.conf [auditTrail] queueing), so the session records are searchable from startup rather than only written to the audit log file.
citation: SRG-APP-000092-AU-000670 check text; audit.conf.spec:23-29 ([auditTrail], queueing = <boolean>, "If set to false, you must add an inputs.conf stanza to tail the audit log", Default: true); audit.conf.spec:6-8 (there is no default audit.conf; custom settings are placed in a local audit.conf)

conditions.rationale: The spec states that when true audit events are sent to the indexQueue, and that when false "you must add an inputs.conf stanza to tail the audit log for the events [to] reach your index"; queueing true is what makes session auditing effective from splunkd startup. Default is true, so an unmodified instance satisfies the condition.

external_dependencies: The operating system's service manager must start splunkd at boot (a systemd unit or Splunk boot-start), which determines when auditing actually begins; "upon startup" is bounded by that and is not an application setting.

If queueing is deliberately set to false, the compensating inputs.conf stanza that tails the audit log is the assessable alternative; that is a separate input definition rather than a value of this key.
finding_statement: audit.conf [auditTrail] queueing is set to false and no input tails the audit log, so the session audit events splunkd generates at startup do not reach an index.

application_contribution: Splunk Web opens its HTTP access log when the application server starts, and splunkd records REST access in splunkd_access.log from the same moment; the application configures which log receives that traffic and that no endpoint is excluded from it.
citation: INVENTION. Removed web.conf [settings] appServerPorts not_equals 0. web.conf.spec defines the setting as "appServerPorts = <positive integer>[, <positive integer>...]" and states "At one time, setting this to zero indicated that the web service should be run in a legacy mode as a separate service, but as of Splunk 8.0 this is no longer supported." Zero is outside the permitted vocabulary on 10.4.2, so the condition tests a state the product cannot be in and contributes no evidence; neither the check nor the fix text mentions it. The restmap placeholder stanza was replaced with the empty stanza the determined row carries.

conditions.rationale: web.conf.spec: "log.access_file = <filename> * The HTTP access log filename... Default: web_access.log" - the log the web tier opens at startup must be named.

restmap.conf.spec: "Whether to include requests to this endpoint in the splunkd_access.log... If set to \"false\", requests do not appear in splunkd_access.log. Default: true" - an endpoint set to false is silently omitted from the log that begins at startup.

external_dependencies: The operating system's service manager decides when splunkd and Splunk Web start, so whether logging begins at system boot depends on the boot-start configuration, not on the application.
finding_statement: The web tier's access logging is not fully configured - no access log is named, or a REST endpoint is excluded from splunkd_access.log - so logging does not capture all requests from the moment the application server starts.

application_contribution: Splunk sets retention per index: frozenTimePeriodInSecs is the retention period in seconds, so the product can express whatever period the organization documents.
citation: DIRECTION, inverted. Removed authorize.conf [role_user] indexes_edit absent. The check text reads "Verify the SA and ISSM have been assigned the privileges needed to allow these roles to change the level and type of log records that are retained", and CCI-001914 is a provision requirement - the capability must exist for the named roles. Withholding indexes_edit from the ordinary user role is the opposite test, and it passes vacuously anyway: the shipped [role_user] in system/default/authorize.conf does not list indexes_edit, so the condition reports compliant without any evidence that the required privilege exists. A positive condition is not a sound replacement either, because authorize.conf.spec accepts only "enabled" for a capability and the product ships indexes_edit = enabled under [role_admin], so such a condition could never fail. The privilege question is therefore recorded as an external dependency.

conditions.rationale: SPLK-CL-000120 fix text: "Set frozenTimePeriodInSecs to the defined retention period for each index location"; its check text compares the setting against the site documentation, so the criterion tests only that the product expresses the period.

external_dependencies: The documented retention period, criticality levels and event types are organization-defined; SPLK-CL-000120 compares frozenTimePeriodInSecs against the site documentation, which the application cannot supply.
Assignment of the SA and ISSM to a Splunk role that holds indexes_edit is account provisioning and ISSM appointment; authorize.conf records a role's capabilities, not who holds the role.
finding_statement: No retention period is expressed for the indexes in scope (frozenTimePeriodInSecs is not set), so the retention the organization documented by criticality level, event type and period is not configured in the product.

application_contribution: Splunk stamps every indexed record with the sourcetype assigned to its input, which is the record's event type, and its own audit records reach a searchable index when the audit trail is queued to the index.
citation: OVER-REACH and INVENTION. Removed eventtypes.conf [<eventtype>] search non_empty: the shipped eventtypes.conf declares "search =" empty in its default stanza and ships no event types, so the condition fails a stock instance that nonetheless stamps a sourcetype on every record; event types are an optional search-time classification feature and neither the check nor the fix text requires them. Also removed props.conf [<spec>] <spec> present, which named the spec-file placeholder as both stanza and key: props.conf has no setting of that name, so the condition could never match, and the determined row is a whole-file presence test that every installation passes.

conditions.rationale: The sourcetype assigned per data input is the attribute by which Splunk establishes what kind of record it received and selects the props.conf stanza that parses it.

audit.conf.spec: "Whether or not audit events are sent to the indexQueue... If set to \"false\", you must add an inputs.conf stanza to tail the audit log for the events reach your index. Default: true."

external_dependencies: The originating hosts and devices must emit an event type or category in the records they transmit; Splunk classifies what it receives and cannot add a type the sender omitted.
finding_statement: Splunk does not establish the type of each record it holds - inputs have no sourcetype assigned, or the audit trail is not queued to an index - so the event type cannot be determined from the stored records.

application_contribution: Splunk's web tier records the request method, URI and target endpoint - the event type for a web transaction - in web_access.log and splunkd_access.log, and the application configures that those logs are written and that no endpoint is excluded.
citation: INVENTION. Removed web.conf [settings] log.access_maxfiles min 1. web.conf.spec defines it as "The maximum number of backup files to keep after the web_access.log file has reached its maximum size" - a rotation-retention count that has no bearing on what information each record contains. The type is <integer>, so 0 is permitted, and an instance keeping no backups still records the request method and URI in the current log; the condition would fail a configuration that satisfies the objective. Neither the check nor the fix text mentions log rotation. The restmap placeholder stanza was replaced with the empty stanza the determined row carries.

conditions.rationale: web.conf.spec: "log.access_file = <filename> * The HTTP access log filename... Default: web_access.log" - the log that carries the request method and URI must be named.
restmap.conf.spec: an endpoint set to "false" does not appear in splunkd_access.log, so the type of request made to it is not recorded anywhere.

external_dependencies: The record layout of the splunk_web_access and splunkd_access sourcetypes is built into the product and is not a props.conf setting in the 10.4.2 specification, so the fields present in a written record are confirmed by inspecting one.
finding_statement: The web tier does not record what type of request occurred - no access log is named, or a REST endpoint is excluded from splunkd_access.log - so the event type for those transactions cannot be established.

application_contribution: Splunk assigns _time to every indexed record, and DATETIME_CONFIG selects whether that time is extracted from the record's own text or replaced by the server's processing time.
citation: DIRECTION. Removed props.conf MAX_TIMESTAMP_LOOKAHEAD min 1. props.conf.spec states "If set to 0 or -1, the length constraint for timestamp recognition is effectively disabled" - 0 and -1 remove the character limit so the extractor scans the whole event, which recognizes timestamps at least as well as the default of 128, not worse. The condition reads those values as if they switched timestamping off, so it fails exactly the configurations it should pass. The setting bounds a search window for performance and appears in neither the check nor the fix text.

conditions.rationale: props.conf.spec: "Both 'CURRENT' and 'NONE' explicitly disable the per-text timestamp identification"; CURRENT "sets the time of the event to the time that the event was merged from lines" and NONE "leaves the event time set to whatever time was selected by the input layer", neither of which is when the event occurred.

external_dependencies: The accuracy of the recorded time rests on host clock synchronization, performed by the operating system's time service and assessed under SRG-APP-000086-AU-000030.
finding_statement: Timestamp extraction is disabled for the sourcetypes in scope (DATETIME_CONFIG set to NONE or CURRENT), so the time on a stored record is when Splunk processed it rather than when the event occurred.

application_contribution: Every record Splunk's web tier writes to web_access.log and splunkd_access.log begins with a date and time that no setting suppresses; what the application configures is that those logs are written.
citation: SCOPE and INVENTION. Removed props.conf [<spec>] TZ present. TZ is an index-time setting that assigns a time zone to data Splunk ingests; it does not govern what the web tier writes into its own access logs, which is what this requirement covers. props.conf.spec also gives "Default: empty string" and a documented fallback chain - a zone in the record's raw text, then TZ, then the forwarder's zone, then "the timezone of the system that is running splunkd" - so an unset TZ is a supported configuration and requiring it would fail a correct instance. The condition also contradicted the criterion's own statement that the timestamp is emitted unconditionally.

conditions.rationale: web.conf.spec: "log.access_file = <filename> * The HTTP access log filename... Default: web_access.log" - the log whose records carry the date and time must be named.

external_dependencies: The timestamp itself is emitted unconditionally by the product at the start of each record in both access logs, so that part of the objective has no configuration surface and is confirmed by inspecting a written record.
finding_statement: No HTTP access log is named in web.conf, so the web tier writes no record for the date and time of each event to appear on.

application_contribution: Splunk stamps host, source, sourcetype and index on every record it indexes. The application assigns the destination index and the sourcetype per data input, and derives the host either statically (inputs.conf host) or from the path of the file being read (host_regex, host_segment), so each record states where it came from and where it is held.
citation: SRG-APP-000097-AU-000700 check text; SPLK-CL-000110 fix text; inputs.conf.spec:60 (host = <string>), :93-96 (index = <string>), :113-116 (sourcetype = <string>), :244-262 (host_regex = <regular expression>, host_segment = <integer>)

conditions.rationale: SPLK-CL-000110 fix text directs the operator to configure inputs.conf with the information of the senders; the index names where within the repository the record is held, and leaving it unset places records in the default index implicitly.
The sourcetype identifies which log on the originating system the record came from, which is the 'where' for a record received from a host or device.

external_dependencies: For records arriving over the network the origin is resolved by inputs.conf connection_host, assessed under SRG-APP-000098-AU-000710, and reverse lookups there depend on the DNS service.
The sending host must identify itself in the record or in the Splunk-to-Splunk header; Splunk cannot reconstruct an origin the sender withheld.
Where host_regex or host_segment derives the host from a path, the naming convention of that path is a property of the sending system.
finding_statement: Data inputs in inputs.conf do not assign the destination index and sourcetype, so the records Splunk Enterprise produces do not establish where the event occurred or where it is held.

application_contribution: splunkd_access.log names the REST endpoint that handled each request and web_service.log identifies the Splunk Web process that raised each event; the application configures that no endpoint is omitted from the access log.
citation: INVENTION. Removed web.conf [settings] log.error_maxfiles min 1. web.conf.spec defines it as "The maximum number of backup files to keep after the web_service.log file has reached its maximum size" - how many rotated copies are retained, not whether the process identity is recorded. The type is <integer>, so 0 is permitted, and web_service.log is still written at 0; the condition would fail an instance that satisfies the objective. Neither the check nor the fix text concerns log rotation.

conditions.rationale: restmap.conf.spec: "Whether to include requests to this endpoint in the splunkd_access.log... If set to \"false\", requests do not appear in splunkd_access.log. Default: true" - an excluded endpoint leaves no record of where in the web server the event occurred.

external_dependencies: The endpoint and process identifiers are written by the product in a fixed record format with no configuration surface, so their content is confirmed by inspecting a written record rather than by reading configuration.
finding_statement: A REST endpoint is configured with includeInAccessLog = false, so requests it handles leave no record in splunkd_access.log and the location within the web server where those events occurred cannot be established.

application_contribution: For records that arrive without a host already set, Splunk derives the origin from the sending system: connection_host = ip uses the sender's address and dns uses its reverse DNS name.
citation: Unmatchable condition corrected. The original stanza [<network input stanza>] is prose, not a stanza name, and assess.sh compares stanza names literally, so the condition never matched and the row returned absent on every instance. The determined row carries no stanza, and connection_host occurs only in network input stanzas (tcp, udp, splunktcp and their token variants, and [http://name] for HEC), so the key scopes the condition without a stanza. Qualifier for the assessor: inputs.conf.spec says "none" leaves the host "as specified in inputs.conf", so where none is paired with an explicit per-input host the origin is still established; read inputs.conf host before citing this, as ANDed conditions cannot express that pairing.

conditions.rationale: inputs.conf.spec: "A value of \"none\" leaves the host as specified in inputs.conf, typically the hostname of the system running Splunk software" - the receiver's own name, which does not establish the source of the event.

external_dependencies: Reverse DNS correctness where connection_host = dns rests on the DNS service; the specification requires the forward lookup to match the reverse lookup.
Hosts forwarding over the Splunk-to-Splunk protocol set the host on the sending side, and connection_host applies only where the sender leaves it unset.
finding_statement: A network input is configured with connection_host = none and no explicit host, so records arriving on it are stamped with the log server's own hostname and the source of the event cannot be established.

application_contribution: Splunk's web access logs record the client address of every request. The application controls that those logs are written and that no REST endpoint is excluded from them; where a reverse proxy fronts the instance, tools.proxy.on makes all of its HTTP services take the client address from the X-Forwarded-* headers instead of the proxy's own.
citation: SRG-APP-000098-WSR-000059 check text; web.conf.spec:871-874 (log.access_file = <filename>, Default: web_access.log), :797-804 (trustedIP = <ip_addresses>), :1016-1033 (tools.proxy.on = <boolean>, Default: false; tools.proxy.base = <scheme>://<URL>, Default: empty string); restmap.conf.spec:138-142 (includeInAccessLog = <boolean>, Default: true)

conditions.rationale: The access log is where the source address of each Splunk Web request is recorded; an empty filename leaves no such record.
An endpoint set to false produces no splunkd_access.log entry, so the source of requests to it cannot be established. Default is true.

external_dependencies: Where a proxy or load balancer fronts the instance, the client address must be inserted by that device in X-Forwarded-For; that case and the matching tools.proxy settings are assessed under SRG-APP-000098-WSR-000060.
The source address field is emitted by the product in a fixed record format with no configuration surface.
finding_statement: Splunk Enterprise has no web access log configured, or excludes REST endpoints from splunkd_access.log, so the records available do not establish the source of web events.

application_contribution: Where a reverse proxy or load balancer fronts the instance, Splunk can be told so: tools.proxy.on makes its HTTP services use the X-Forwarded-* headers for access request logging instead of the immediate client's address.
citation: SCOPE drift within the product, and OVER-REACH. Removed inputs.conf [http://<name>] connection_host equals proxied_ip. That setting governs how the HTTP Event Collector stamps host on ingested events - inputs.conf.spec documents proxied_ip only in the [http://name] token stanza, where it "checks whether an X-Forwarded-For header was sent... and if so, sets the host to that value" - which is data ingestion, not the web server's own access logging that this requirement covers. An instance with no HEC token input, or whose HEC is not fronted by the proxy, would be failed for a control it satisfies. The determined row also carries no stanza, so the placeholder could not have matched.
external_dependencies: Whether a proxy or load balancer fronts the instance decides whether this requirement applies at all - the check text makes it not applicable otherwise - and that is read from the network architecture documentation.
The fronting proxy must insert the client address in an X-Forwarded-For header; Splunk can only consume a header the device sends.

Whether a reverse proxy or load balancer fronts this instance at all, which decides whether the requirement has a configuration surface here; where one is present, web.conf [settings] tools.proxy.on must be true and tools.proxy.base must carry a scheme as well as a host and port.
The proxy's own insertion of the X-Forwarded-For header, without which tools.proxy.on has no client address to record.
finding_statement: The instance is fronted by a proxy or load balancer but tools.proxy.on is not enabled with a tools.proxy.base, so its access records carry the proxy's address rather than the client's.
manual_reason: The requirement applies to a web server that sits behind a load balancer or proxy server, and it asks that the access record carry the client address rather than the proxy address. web.conf [settings] tools.proxy.on and tools.proxy.base tell Splunk Web that a proxy is in front of it, so they are correctly unset where none is, and asserting them unconditionally reports a finding against an instance that is reached directly. Whether a proxy fronts the instance is an architecture fact outside the configuration, so the assessor establishes that first and then reads the two settings.

application_contribution: Splunk's own audit records carry the outcome of each audited operation and reach a searchable index when the audit trail is queued to the index.
citation: OVER-REACH and INVENTION, as at SRG-APP-000095-AU-000680. Removed eventtypes.conf [<eventtype>] search non_empty: the shipped eventtypes.conf declares "search =" empty in its default stanza and ships no event types, so the condition fails a stock instance; event types are an optional search-time feature that neither the check nor the fix text requires. Also removed props.conf [<spec>] <spec> present, which named the spec-file placeholder as both stanza and key - props.conf has no such setting, so it could never match - and whose determined form is a whole-file presence test every installation passes. Outcome is carried in the record text and read by field extraction, which no single props.conf key decides.

conditions.rationale: audit.conf.spec: "Whether or not audit events are sent to the indexQueue. If set to \"true\", audit events are sent to the indexQueue. If set to \"false\", you must add an inputs.conf stanza to tail the audit log for the events reach your index. Default: true."

external_dependencies: The sending hosts and devices must state the outcome in the records they transmit; Splunk extracts and classifies what it receives and cannot infer an outcome the sender omitted.
Where queueing is deliberately set to false, the audit log is still written to disk and the records reach an index only through a separate monitor input, which the assessor confirms in inputs.conf.
finding_statement: The audit trail is not queued to an index (queueing = false) with no compensating input, so the outcome recorded on each audited operation is not searchable in the repository.

application_contribution: Every record in web_access.log and splunkd_access.log carries the HTTP status code, which is the outcome of the request. The application controls that those logs are written (log.access_file), that no REST endpoint is excluded from them (includeInAccessLog), and that rotated copies are retained; the status field itself is emitted unconditionally.
citation: SRG-APP-000099-WSR-000061 check text; web.conf.spec:871-874 (log.access_file = <filename>, Default: web_access.log), :891-898 (log.error_maxsize = <integer>, Default: 25000000); restmap.conf.spec:138-142 (includeInAccessLog = <boolean>, Default: true)

conditions.rationale: The access log is the record that carries the HTTP status - success or failure - of each Splunk Web request; an empty filename leaves no such record.
An endpoint set to false produces no splunkd_access.log entry, so the outcome of requests to it is not recorded. Default is true.

external_dependencies: The HTTP status code is emitted by the product in a fixed record format with no configuration surface, so its presence is confirmed by inspecting a written record.
The check text's observation step - a user generating events and the logs then being reviewed - is procedural.
finding_statement: Splunk Enterprise has no web access log configured, or excludes REST endpoints from splunkd_access.log, so the records available do not establish the success or failure of web events.

application_contribution: Every Splunk audit record names the account that performed the operation, and those records reach a searchable index when the audit trail is queued to the index.
citation: Three conditions removed. savedsearches.conf dispatchAs in user|owner is the setting's entire permitted vocabulary - savedsearches.conf.spec gives "dispatchAs = [user|owner]" - so it cannot fail and is not evidence; the substantive value is "user", since "owner" runs a shared search "as if the owner of the search dispatched the search, no matter which user requested it", but the same spec notes that limits.conf force_saved_search_dispatch_as_user = true resets dispatchAs to user, a disjunction ANDed conditions cannot express, so it is left to inspection rather than asserted wrongly. authorize.conf [role_<roleName>] role_<roleName> present and props.conf [<spec>] <spec> present both name a placeholder as a key that no such setting exists for; in their determined form they are presence tests that every installation passes.

conditions.rationale: audit.conf.spec: "Whether or not audit events are sent to the indexQueue... If set to \"false\", you must add an inputs.conf stanza to tail the audit log for the events reach your index. Default: true."
